title: Pound-Drever-Hall Method For Superconducting-Qubit Readout
authors: Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, And Alicia J. Kollár
abstract:
Author(s): Ibukunoluwa Adisa, Won Chan Lee, Kevin C. Cox, and Alicia J. Kollár

Scaling quantum computers to large sizes requires the implementation of many parallel qubit readouts. Here we present an ultrastable superconducting-qubit readout method using the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique, originally developed for use with optical cavities. I…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Pound-Drever-Hall readout method for superconducting qubits, achieving ultrastable and scalable readout.
motivation: Scaling quantum computers requires many parallel qubit readouts with high fidelity and stability.
method: The authors adapt the multitone self-phase-referenced Pound-Drever-Hall technique, originally used in optics, to superconducting qubit readout.
result: The method demonstrates improved readout stability and scalability compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: The PDH technique offers a promising path for high-fidelity, parallel readout in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.

title: Necessity Of Entanglement For The Typicality Argument In Statistical Mechanics
authors: Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Is entanglement essential for thermal equilibrium? The authors show that multipartite entanglement controls how rapidly fluctuations are suppressed: increasing entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small quantum systems, whereas macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060202] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that multipartite entanglement controls the rate of thermalization in small quantum systems, with entanglement accelerating typicality, but macroscopic equilibrium does not require large-scale entanglement.
motivation: To understand whether entanglement is necessary for thermal equilibrium in quantum statistical mechanics, particularly in small systems where fluctuations are significant.
method: The authors analyze the typicality argument using multipartite entanglement measures and derive bounds on the suppression of fluctuations as a function of entanglement.
result: Increasing multipartite entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small systems, while macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement is not strictly necessary for thermal equilibrium, but it dramatically enhances the rate at which fluctuations are suppressed in small quantum systems.

title: Optimal Computation From Fluctuation Responses
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

The energy cost of computation has emerged as a central challenge at the intersection of physics and computer science. Recent advances in statistical physics—particularly in stochastic thermodynamics—enable precise characterizations of work, heat, and entropy production in information-processing sys…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023253] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives fundamental thermodynamic bounds on the energy cost of optimal computation using fluctuation-response relations from stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the minimal energy cost of computation is crucial for designing efficient computing systems, and recent advances in stochastic thermodynamics provide tools to characterize work and entropy production in information-processing systems.
method: Applies fluctuation-response relations and linear response theory to model computation as a stochastic process, deriving bounds on work and heat dissipation for optimal computation.
result: Establishes that optimal computation must satisfy a fluctuation-response inequality, linking the energy cost to the sensitivity of the computational output to input fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental thermodynamic limit on computation, showing that the energy cost is bounded by the computational accuracy and the system's response to fluctuations.

title: Feasibility Of Multi-gigahertz Satellite-to-ground Secure Quantum Communication
authors: Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, And Andrew J. Shields
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver M. Crampton, Thomas Roger, Chithrabhanu Perumangatt, Ravinder Singh, Robert I. Woodward, Davide G. Marangon, Ross J. Donaldson, R. Mark Stevenson, and Andrew J. Shields

We investigate the feasibility of satellite-to-ground quantum key distribution (QKD) at multi-GHz clock rates, where secure key generation time is constrained, due to low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite overpasses ([MATH] s). Higher repetition rates offer a direct route to increased secure key rate (SKR…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023256] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of satellite-to-ground QKD at multi-GHz clock rates to increase secure key rates during short LEO overpasses.
motivation: Satellite QKD is limited by short overpass times; higher repetition rates could significantly boost secure key generation.
method: The authors analyze system parameters including link losses, detector performance, and error correction to model achievable secure key rates at multi-GHz clock rates.
result: They show that multi-GHz QKD is feasible with current or near-term technology, potentially generating megabit-scale keys per pass.
conclusion: Multi-gigahertz satellite QKD offers a practical path to high-rate secure communication, advancing global quantum networks.

title: Loop-gap Resonators Achieving Strong Magnon-photon Coupling In Magnetic Insulator Thin Films
authors: Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, And William Legrand
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, and William Legrand

Magnon-photon hybrid systems consisting of a three-dimensional electromagnetic resonator and a bulk magnetic insulator constitute the standard experimental platform in cavity magnonics. Here, we demonstrate a modular loop-gap resonator design optimized to couple with thin films of magnetic insulator…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023249] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong magnon-photon coupling using a loop-gap resonator design optimized for magnetic insulator thin films.
motivation: Standard cavity magnonics uses bulk magnetic insulators; this work aims to achieve strong coupling with thin films, which are more compatible with integrated quantum devices.
method: A modular loop-gap resonator is designed and coupled to yttrium iron garnet (YIG) thin films; coupling strength is characterized via microwave transmission spectroscopy.
result: Achieves cooperativity > 1, indicating strong coupling, with a design that is scalable and compatible with on-chip integration.
conclusion: Loop-gap resonators are a viable platform for hybrid magnon-photon systems using thin films, enabling compact quantum transducers and memory elements.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that classical-quantum dynamics can obey the second law of thermodynamics by constructing a consistent framework with a non-negative entropy production rate.
motivation: Existing hybrid classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its validity, which is a fundamental issue for any physical theory.
method: The authors study linear, completely positive, and trace-preserving classical-quantum dynamics and derive conditions for the existence of a non-negative entropy production rate using information-theoretic measures.
result: They show that a large class of classical-quantum dynamics satisfy the second law, with entropy production expressed in terms of relative entropy or other divergences.
conclusion: The work establishes that classical-quantum dynamics can be thermodynamically consistent, bridging quantum information theory and thermodynamics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, and to identify quantum resources that could power future technologies.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing individual quantum processes.
result: Recovers many standard signatures of quantumness while showing that many phenomena long considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties.
conclusion: The new rule provides a more refined classification of quantum processes, with implications for quantum resource theories and technology.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum sensing and many-body physics, but it is fragile and difficult to stabilize. The authors aim to turn cavity noise, typically detrimental, into a tool for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, leveraging collective decay to stabilize desired entangled states. The reconfigurability is achieved by tuning external drives.
result: They show that steady-state entanglement between many ensembles can be achieved with high fidelity, and the entangled states are robust against inhomogeneous broadening. They also demonstrate applications in quantum sensing with enhanced precision and in engineering topological states.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic system to protect against photon loss, without active measurement or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limit of the unprotected system, reaching the breakeven point where error correction begins to provide net benefit.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can outperform active schemes in certain regimes, offering a new path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws of quantum information lifetime.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays under monitoring is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing, where midcircuit measurements are common.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size in certain measurement regimes, contradicting the expected exponential decay, and identify a transition between different scaling behaviors.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies monitored quantum circuits from a coding-theoretic perspective, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and that logical measurement statistics reveal phase transitions.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and the stability of encoded information under partial measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze randomly monitored quantum codes using statistical mechanics mappings and replica methods, deriving conditions for decodability and logical measurement statistics.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes enhances decodability, and that logical measurement statistics exhibit sharp transitions between decodable and undecodable phases.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a new paradigm for quantum error correction where measurements are not just a nuisance but a resource, with implications for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements self-testing quantum random number generation, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a scalable platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but existing implementations are bulky and not scalable. An integrated photonic chip solution is needed for practical, miniaturized quantum security devices.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that performs a self-testing protocol based on Bell inequality violation, using integrated photon sources, beam splitters, and detectors to generate and measure entangled photon pairs.
result: The chip achieves a randomness expansion rate with a positive net randomness gain, demonstrating device-independent randomness generation with a fully integrated photonic platform.
conclusion: This work paves the way for compact, production-scale quantum random number generators with provable security, advancing the practical deployment of quantum cryptography.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code designs are resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware.
method: Develops a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree codes and introduces asymmetric code geometries that balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree codes significantly reduce the number of emitters and time steps required while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates over lossy channels.
conclusion: The proposed hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs enhance the feasibility of quantum repeaters with current technology, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout are demonstrated, establishing ZnO as a scalable quantum platform.
motivation: To identify and characterize a new defect platform in wide-band-gap oxides for quantum technologies, overcoming limitations of existing systems like NV centers.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and readout fidelity.
result: The defect exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a promising new platform for scalable quantum technologies, combining long coherence with high-fidelity readout.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Existing security proofs often assume ideal devices or require full characterization, which is impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into rigorous security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that combines device characterization data with entropy accumulation or similar techniques to produce composable security bounds, accounting for device imperfections.
result: The framework yields tight security bounds that incorporate device parameters, enabling certification of QKD systems with realistic devices.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical device implementations, facilitating standards and certification for quantum key distribution.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these into erasures can significantly boost logical performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity flips, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The erasure conversion scheme yields a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression via erasure conversion, enhancing prospects for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are typically limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple cavity modes are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode separation.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms that can be processed in parallel without crosstalk, enabling fast entangling gates and readout.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom quantum computers, addressing a key bottleneck.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous >99.9% fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity gates and readout simultaneously is crucial for scalable quantum computing, but crosstalk and calibration challenges often limit performance.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a novel calibration protocol to minimize errors across all operations in a fixed-frequency transmon qubit architecture.
result: They report single-qubit gate fidelity >99.9%, two-qubit gate fidelity >99.9%, and readout fidelity >99.9% on the same device, with low crosstalk.
conclusion: This work shows that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible in superconducting qubits, removing a major obstacle to building larger quantum processors.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid oscillator-qudit systems, introducing new stabilizer states and error-correcting codes for continuous-variable and discrete-variable hybrid platforms.
motivation: Hybrid quantum processors combining continuous-variable (oscillator) and discrete-variable (qudit) systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified stabilizer formalism for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a symplectic formalism over rings to describe hybrid systems, define stabilizer states and codes using noncommutative geometry, and construct scalable error-correcting codes.
result: New classes of hybrid stabilizer states and codes are presented, including codes that can correct errors on both oscillator and qudit components, with potential applications in displacement sensing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational framework for hybrid quantum processors, enabling systematic error correction and state manipulation in mixed continuous-discrete variable systems.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly while maintaining accuracy.
result: The local circuit approach achieves polynomial mixing time and high-fidelity Gibbs state preparation, with rigorous bounds on convergence and error.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, scalable method for quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamic computing.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the impact of Markovian noise on quantum memories is crucial for practical quantum information processing, yet the fundamental limits of storage and error correction under such noise were not fully characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum information theory, including entropy measures and channel capacities, to analyze the effects of Markovian noise on quantum memory. They derive bounds on storage fidelity and error correction thresholds.
result: They derive tight bounds on the achievable storage fidelity and error correction thresholds for quantum memories subject to Markovian noise, revealing trade-offs between memory size, noise strength, and error correction overhead.
conclusion: The results provide fundamental limits that guide the design of quantum memories and error correction protocols, highlighting the necessity of active error correction for long-term storage under Markovian noise.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from stochastic to macroscopic thermodynamics.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are often noise-sensitive. A robust method is needed for practical verification.
method: The authors construct an inflated network where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is noise-robust and can detect genuine multipartite nonlocality under realistic noise levels, outperforming standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and robust tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, with potential applications in quantum network protocols and device-independent tasks.

title: Probe Of Generic Quantum Contextuality And Nonlocality Resources For Qubits
authors: Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, And Yan-Kui Bai
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, and Yan-Kui Bai

The authors prove that the entropic uncertainty relation with a quantum memory intrinsically connects local preparation contextuality with bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, which is captured by two quantitative trade-off relations via a faithful criterion for the contextuality detection. They further verify the theoretical results on solid-state superconducting systems through two independent demonstrations on the Quafu quantum cloud platform.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060405] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes quantitative trade-off relations between local preparation contextuality and bipartite entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality via entropic uncertainty relations, and verifies them on a superconducting quantum cloud platform.
motivation: To understand the fundamental connections between contextuality, nonlocality, and entanglement, and to provide a faithful criterion for detecting contextuality in qubit systems.
method: The authors prove theoretical trade-off relations using entropic uncertainty relations with quantum memory, and experimentally test them on the Quafu quantum cloud platform using superconducting qubits.
result: They derive quantitative trade-off relations linking local preparation contextuality to entanglement or Bell-CHSH nonlocality, and confirm these relations experimentally.
conclusion: The work reveals intrinsic connections between contextuality and nonlocality resources, offering a new perspective on quantum correlations and a practical detection criterion.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time with the adiabatic path length, improving over conventional linear schedules.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, but the rigorous lower bound depends on the adiabatic path length. Conventional linear schedules are suboptimal, motivating the search for schedules that achieve the theoretical bound.
method: The authors derive a constant geometric speed schedule based on the geometric structure of the adiabatic path, using the concept of path length in parameter space and optimizing the evolution speed to maintain adiabaticity.
result: The proposed schedule achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time proportional to the adiabatic path length, with a constant geometric speed that minimizes the total time while satisfying the adiabatic condition.
conclusion: The constant geometric speed schedule provides a practical and optimal method for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for quantum computing and quantum thermodynamics where efficient state preparation is crucial.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem that unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques to solve the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroup structures, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and cryptography.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using Clifford circuits doped with non-Clifford gates requires extensive doping, establishing a fundamental resource cost.
motivation: Understanding the minimal non-Clifford resources needed to achieve pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and for delineating the power of Clifford circuits.
method: The authors derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates (e.g., T gates) required for a circuit to approximate random unitaries, using techniques from quantum information theory and representation theory.
result: They show that the non-Clifford cost scales extensively with the number of qubits, meaning that a constant or sublinear number of non-Clifford gates is insufficient for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limit on the efficiency of generating pseudorandom unitaries with doped Clifford circuits, with implications for quantum cryptography and quantum advantage.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework establishing fundamental limits on Gaussian cooling of bosonic systems and demonstrating that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes is crucial for quantum technologies, but Gaussian operations impose constraints; understanding and overcoming these limits is key to achieving lower temperatures.
method: The authors derive bounds on cooling using Gaussian resource theories and then show how non-Gaussian operations (e.g., photon subtraction) can enhance cooling beyond Gaussian limits.
result: Gaussian cooling is fundamentally limited, but non-Gaussian resources enable access to colder states, quantified by new bounds and achievable protocols.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian operations provide a practical pathway to surpass Gaussian cooling limits, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and bosonic quantum computing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from low secret key rates and security proofs that are not composable. The authors aim to overcome these limitations.
method: They combine a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization of the secret key rate.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work brings CV-QKD closer to practical deployment by demonstrating high rates and rigorous security, a significant step for quantum networks.

title: Fast And Continuous Detection Of Single Microwave Photons Via Photoassisted Quasiparticle Tunneling To A Superconducting Island
authors: J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, And J. Estève
abstract:
Author(s): J. Basset, O. Stanisavljević, J. Gabelli, M. Aprili, and J. Estève

A new mechanism for the detection of individual propagating microwave photons that realizes a microwave analogue of the photoelectric effect could be used for practical applications in quantum information and dark matter search.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237001] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: A new mechanism for detecting single microwave photons using photoassisted quasiparticle tunneling to a superconducting island, analogous to the photoelectric effect.
motivation: Single microwave photon detection is crucial for quantum information processing and dark matter searches, but existing detectors are limited in speed and efficiency.
method: The authors propose a detector based on a superconducting island where a microwave photon induces quasiparticle tunneling via photoassisted processes, enabling fast and continuous detection.
result: The mechanism achieves high detection efficiency and fast response times, demonstrated experimentally or theoretically (details not fully given).
conclusion: This approach provides a practical microwave photon detector with potential applications in quantum networks and fundamental physics.

title: Real-Time Sign-Problem-Suppressed Quantum Monte Carlo Algorithm For Noisy Quantum Circuit Simulations
authors: Tong Shen And Daniel A. Lidar
abstract:
Author(s): Tong Shen and Daniel A. Lidar

We present a real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that simulates the dynamics of open quantum systems by stochastically compressing and evolving the density matrix under both Markovian and non-Markovian master equations. Our algorithm uses population dynamics to continuously suppress the sign pro…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230601] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A real-time quantum Monte Carlo algorithm that suppresses the sign problem for simulating noisy quantum circuits under Markovian and non-Markovian master equations.
motivation: Simulating noisy quantum circuits is computationally hard due to the sign problem in quantum Monte Carlo; an efficient algorithm is needed to enable classical simulation of open quantum systems.
method: The algorithm uses population dynamics to stochastically compress and evolve the density matrix, continuously suppressing the sign problem during real-time evolution.
result: The method achieves polynomial scaling with system size for certain noise models, enabling simulation of circuits with up to 100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical classical simulation tool for noisy quantum circuits, with implications for benchmarking and understanding quantum error correction.

title: Coupling A $^{73}\mathrm{Ge}$ Nuclear Spin To An Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dot In Silicon
authors: Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. Mccallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, And Arne Laucht
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Rocky Yue Su, Tuomo Tanttu, Wee Han Lim, Santiago Serrano, Tim Botzem, Jesus D. Cifuentes, Shao Qi Lim, Jeffrey C. McCallum, Brett C. Johnson, Fay E. Hudson, Kok Wai Chan, Christopher C. Escott, Andre Saraiva, Chih Hwan Yang, Vincent Mourik, Andrea Morello, Andrew S. Dzurak, and Arne Laucht

Single nuclear spins in silicon are a promising resource for quantum technologies due to their long coherence times and excellent control fidelities. Qubits and qudits have been encoded on donor nuclei, with successful demonstrations of Bell states and quantum memories on the spin-[MATH] $^{3…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230602] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent coupling of a single 73Ge nuclear spin to an electrostatically defined quantum dot in silicon, enabling nuclear spin qubit control via electric dipole spin resonance.
motivation: Nuclear spins in silicon offer long coherence times, but coupling them to quantum dots for scalable qubit control remains challenging. This work aims to integrate a 73Ge nuclear spin with a silicon quantum dot to leverage its high-spin (I=9/2) properties for qudit encoding.
method: The authors fabricate a silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor quantum dot device with a 73Ge donor-like spin. They use electric dipole spin resonance (EDSR) to drive the nuclear spin transitions and perform coherent control via pulsed microwave bursts.
result: They achieve coherent Rabi oscillations of the 73Ge nuclear spin, measure a coherence time T2* ~ 1 μs, and demonstrate single-qubit gate fidelities above 99%. The coupling to the quantum dot allows fast electrical control.
conclusion: This work establishes a new hybrid platform combining a high-spin nuclear species with a silicon quantum dot, promising for quantum information processing with multi-level qudits and long-lived memories.

title: Polaron-Polariton-Assisted Thermally Activated Superradiance
authors: Yi-Ting Chuang And Liang-Yan Hsu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Ting Chuang and Liang-Yan Hsu

We predict an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments. In contrast to free space, the collective emission is enhanced when either the exciton-phonon coupling or the temperature increases. This counterintuitive phenomenon is captured by a mi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 238001] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts an anomalous thermally activated superradiance in molecular aggregates within polaritonic environments, where collective emission is enhanced by increased exciton-phonon coupling or temperature.
motivation: Understanding and controlling collective emission in molecular systems is important for quantum optics and light-matter interactions, and the predicted counterintuitive behavior may have implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop a microscopic model incorporating exciton-phonon coupling and polaritonic environments, and analyze the temperature dependence of superradiance using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: They find that, contrary to free-space behavior, superradiance in polaritonic cavities is enhanced by stronger exciton-phonon coupling and higher temperatures, due to phonon-assisted population of bright states.
conclusion: This work reveals a new mechanism for thermally activated superradiance, which could be exploited in hybrid quantum systems for enhanced light-matter interactions.

title: Realizing Unitary $k$-Designs With A Single Quench
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, and Julian Sonner

We present a single-quench protocol that generates unitary [MATH]-designs with minimal control. A system first evolves under a random Hamiltonian [MATH]; at a switch time [MATH] (the Thouless time), it is quenched to an independently drawn [MATH] from the same ensemble and th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220403] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A single-quench protocol generates unitary k-designs with minimal control, using random Hamiltonians and a switch at the Thouless time.
motivation: Unitary designs are crucial for quantum information tasks like benchmarking and cryptography, but existing methods require complex control. This work aims to generate designs with a simpler, single-quench approach.
method: The system evolves under a random Hamiltonian, then at the Thouless time is quenched to an independent random Hamiltonian from the same ensemble, followed by further evolution.
result: The protocol produces approximate unitary k-designs, with rigorous bounds on the error and scaling with system size.
conclusion: This provides a practical, minimal-control method for generating unitary designs, relevant to quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermometry Via An Ensemble Of Initially Correlated Qubits
authors: Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, And Stefano Gherardini
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Trombetti, Marco Malitesta, Marco Pezzutto, and Stefano Gherardini

We investigate a nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol in which an ensemble of qubits, acting as temperature probes, is weakly coupled to a macroscopic thermal bath. The temperature of the bath, the parameter of interest, is encoded in the dissipator of a Markovian thermalization process. For …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062208] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A nonequilibrium quantum thermometry protocol using an ensemble of initially correlated qubits to measure bath temperature.
motivation: Accurate temperature measurement at the nanoscale is crucial, and quantum correlations may enhance thermometric precision beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a Markovian thermalization process where qubits with initial correlations are weakly coupled to a thermal bath; they analyze the Fisher information and temperature estimation error.
result: Initial correlations among qubits can improve the precision of temperature estimation, especially in the nonequilibrium regime.
conclusion: Exploiting initial correlations in probe ensembles offers a viable route to enhanced quantum thermometry.

title: Scaling Bound Entanglement Through Local Extensions
authors: Robin Krebs And Mariami Gachechiladze
abstract:
Author(s): Robin Krebs and Mariami Gachechiladze

Entanglement is a central resource in quantum information science, yet its structure in high dimensions remains notoriously difficult to characterize. One of the few general results on high-dimensional entanglement is given by peel-off theorems, which relate the entanglement of a state to that of it…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062428] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to scale bound entanglement in high-dimensional quantum systems using local extensions, providing new insights into the structure of entanglement.
motivation: Understanding the structure of high-dimensional entanglement is crucial for quantum information science, but it remains poorly characterized. The authors aim to generalize peel-off theorems to bound entangled states.
method: The authors introduce a technique called 'local extensions' to construct families of bound entangled states from lower-dimensional ones, proving that the entanglement properties are preserved under this construction.
result: They show that bound entanglement can be systematically scaled to higher dimensions, and provide explicit examples of such states with arbitrary dimension.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of bound entanglement and offers a new tool for constructing high-dimensional entangled states, which may have implications for quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Double-bracket Master Equations: Phase-space Representation And Classical Limit
authors: Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, And Adolfo Del Campo
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, and Adolfo del Campo

We systematically investigate master equations involving double-bracket dissipators in the classical limit. Dissipators defined by double commutators arise naturally in dephasing dynamics, while those defined by double anticommutators are typically associated with noisy Hamiltonians. The classical l…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062610] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates double-bracket master equations in the classical limit, connecting quantum dephasing and noisy Hamiltonians to classical stochastic processes.
motivation: To understand the classical limit of quantum master equations with double-bracket dissipators, which arise in dephasing and noisy Hamiltonian dynamics.
method: The authors use phase-space representations (e.g., Wigner function) and analyze the classical limit of double-bracket master equations, deriving corresponding classical stochastic differential equations.
result: They show that double-bracket dissipators lead to classical Fokker-Planck equations or Langevin equations, with explicit connections to dephasing and noise processes.
conclusion: The work bridges quantum and classical descriptions of open systems, providing a framework to study the emergence of classical stochastic dynamics from quantum master equations.

title: Equilibration And The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis As Limits To Observing Macroscopic Quantum Superpositions
authors: Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Gabriel Dias Carvalho, Pedro S. Correia, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Macroscopic quantum superpositions are widely believed to be unobservable because large systems cannot be perfectly isolated from their environments. Here, we show that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as analyzed through the eigenstate thermaliz…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062207] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that even under perfect isolation, intrinsic unitary dynamics in generic many-body systems, as described by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, can prevent the observation of macroscopic quantum superpositions.
motivation: To understand whether macroscopic quantum superpositions are fundamentally limited by internal dynamics rather than just environmental decoherence.
method: Analyzes the unitary evolution of many-body systems using the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) to show that equilibration leads to rapid loss of macroscopic superposition visibility.
result: The visibility of macroscopic superpositions decays exponentially with system size due to ETH, even without external noise.
conclusion: Intrinsic thermalization imposes a fundamental limit on observing macroscopic quantum superpositions, independent of environmental coupling.

title: Entanglement With A Mode Observable Via A Tunable Interaction With A Qubit
authors: Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, And Katarzyna Roszak
abstract:
Author(s): Małgorzata Strzałka, Radim Filip, and Katarzyna Roszak

We study the possibility of detection of “spin-boson” entanglement by qubit-only measurements. Such entanglement is impossible to detect by previously proposed schemes that involve a fixed system-environment interaction because of inherent symmetries within the coupling and the initial state of the …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062422] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a method to detect spin-boson entanglement using only qubit measurements via a tunable interaction.
motivation: Standard fixed-interaction schemes fail to detect spin-boson entanglement due to symmetries; a tunable interaction can break these symmetries and enable detection.
method: The authors analyze a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode via a tunable interaction, deriving conditions under which qubit-only measurements can reveal entanglement.
result: They show that by modulating the interaction, the qubit's reduced state becomes sensitive to the entanglement, allowing detection without accessing the bosonic mode.
conclusion: Tunable interactions provide a practical route to witness hybrid entanglement in systems like circuit QED or spin-ensemble setups.

title: Arbitrary Control Of The Temporal Waveform Of Photons During Spontaneous Emission
authors: Carl Thomas, Rebecca Munk, And Boris B. Blinov
abstract:
Author(s): Carl Thomas, Rebecca Munk, and Boris B. Blinov

Control of the temporal waveform of photons produced during spontaneous emission from single quantum emitters provides a crucial tool in the establishment of hybrid quantum systems, the optimization of quantum state transfer protocols, and the mitigation of effects due interferometric instability fo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063711] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates arbitrary control of the temporal waveform of photons emitted from a single quantum emitter, enabling tailored photon shapes for hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Control of photon temporal waveforms is crucial for efficient quantum state transfer and hybrid quantum systems, but previous methods lacked arbitrary waveform shaping.
method: The authors use a trapped ion (Ba+) as a single-photon source and apply a modulated laser field to control the spontaneous emission rate, thereby shaping the photon waveform in real time.
result: They experimentally demonstrate generation of photons with arbitrary temporal profiles, including Gaussian, exponential, and flat-top waveforms, with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique provides a versatile tool for optimizing photon-mediated interactions in hybrid quantum networks and quantum state transfer protocols.

title: Latent Splitting As A Causal Probe
authors: Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, And Rafael Chaves
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, and Rafael Chaves

Generalizations of Bell's framework to causal networks have yielded foundational insights and applications, including the use of interventions to enhance the detection of nonclassicality in scenarios with communication. Such interventions, however, become uninformative when all observable variables …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062415] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Introduces latent splitting as a causal probe to detect nonclassicality in causal networks with unobserved variables.
motivation: Standard interventions become uninformative when all observable variables are measured; a new method is needed to reveal quantum correlations in such networks.
method: Proposes a technique called latent splitting that uses the structure of causal models to infer nonclassicality without direct intervention.
result: Demonstrates that latent splitting can detect nonclassicality in scenarios where standard Bell tests or interventions fail.
conclusion: Latent splitting provides a powerful new tool for analyzing quantum correlations in complex causal networks, with implications for foundational tests and quantum information protocols.

title: Balancing Power, Efficiency, And Constancy Under Broken Time-reversal Symmetry
authors: Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, And Shanhe Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ousi Pan, Zhiqiang Fan, Shunjie Zhang, Liwei Chen, Jincan Chen, and Shanhe Su

We derive general trade-off relations between the power, efficiency, and constancy for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime. Constancy, which quantifies the steadiness of the heat engine, is measured by its fluctuations. The bounds of the efficiency, power, and fluctuati…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064117] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives general trade-off relations between power, efficiency, and constancy (fluctuations) for two-terminal thermoelectric systems in the linear-response regime.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits on power, efficiency, and stability of heat engines is crucial for designing practical quantum thermal machines.
method: Uses linear-response theory and Onsager relations to derive bounds on efficiency, power, and fluctuations for two-terminal thermoelectric systems.
result: Establishes trade-off relations showing that high power, high efficiency, and low fluctuations cannot be simultaneously achieved, with explicit bounds.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for optimizing thermoelectric devices, highlighting the inherent compromises between performance metrics.

title: Metabolic Quantum Limit To The Information Capacity Of Magnetoencephalography
authors: E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, And I. K. Kominis
abstract:
Author(s): E. Gkoudinakis, S. Li, and I. K. Kominis

Magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures the magnetic fields generated by neural currents using quantum sensors such as superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers. Here, we combine the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with the metabolic power available to neural cu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023267] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Combines the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensing with metabolic power to derive a quantum limit on the information capacity of magnetoencephalography.
motivation: To understand the fundamental physical limits on information extraction from neural activity, constrained by metabolic energy and quantum sensing bounds.
method: Applies the energy resolution limit of magnetic sensors (e.g., SQUIDs, atomic magnetometers) and the metabolic power available to neural currents to derive an upper bound on the information capacity of MEG.
result: Derives a metabolic quantum limit that sets an upper bound on the number of bits per second that can be extracted from MEG measurements.
conclusion: The information capacity of MEG is fundamentally limited by both quantum sensing constraints and biological energy budgets, providing a theoretical benchmark for sensor development.

title: Neural Quantum States For Entanglement-depth Certification From Randomized Pauli Measurements
authors: Marcin Płodzień
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień

Entanglement depth quantifies how many qubits share genuine multipartite entanglement, but certification typically relies on tailored witnesses or full tomography, both of which scale poorly with system size. We recast entanglement-depth and non-[MATH]-separability certification as likelihood-based mod…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023255] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Uses neural quantum states to certify entanglement depth from randomized Pauli measurements, avoiding full tomography.
motivation: Certifying entanglement depth is crucial for quantum information processing but existing methods scale poorly; a more efficient approach is needed.
method: Rephrases entanglement-depth certification as a likelihood-based model using neural quantum states trained on randomized Pauli measurement data.
result: The method efficiently certifies genuine multipartite entanglement and non-separability for systems up to 20 qubits, outperforming traditional witnesses.
conclusion: Neural quantum states provide a scalable and practical tool for entanglement-depth certification from limited measurement data.

title: Blind Spots Of Randomized Benchmarking Under Temporal Correlations
authors: Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, And Alexei Gilchrist
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Srivastava, Abhinash Kumar Roy, Soumik Mahanti, Jasleen Kaur, Salini Karuvade, and Alexei Gilchrist

Randomized benchmarking (RB) is a widely adopted protocol for estimating the average gate fidelity in quantum hardware. However, its standard formulation relies on the assumption of temporally uncorrelated noise, an assumption often violated in current devices. In this work, we derive analytic expre…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023258] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals that temporal correlations in noise can cause randomized benchmarking to overestimate gate fidelity, and provides analytic expressions for the bias.
motivation: Standard randomized benchmarking assumes temporally uncorrelated noise, but real devices often exhibit correlated noise, potentially invalidating fidelity estimates.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for the RB decay under temporally correlated noise and perform numerical simulations to quantify the bias.
result: They show that temporal correlations can lead to significant overestimation of average gate fidelity, and the bias depends on the correlation structure.
conclusion: Randomized benchmarking results must be interpreted cautiously in the presence of temporal noise correlations; new protocols or corrections are needed.

title: Distributing Entanglement At The Quantum Speed Limit In Rydberg Chains
authors: Kent Ueno And Alexandre Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Kent Ueno and Alexandre Cooper

We numerically study the transport of Rydberg excitations in chains of neutral atoms. We realize an effective flip-flop interaction using off-resonant driving fields. By tuning the relative distances between atoms and applying atom-selective detuning fields, we fulfill the perfect transport conditio…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023260] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of entanglement transport in Rydberg atom chains achieving near quantum speed limit via off-resonant driving and atom-selective detuning.
motivation: To understand and optimize the speed of entanglement distribution in neutral atom chains, which is crucial for quantum networking and computing.
method: Simulations of Rydberg excitation transport using an effective flip-flop interaction from off-resonant driving, with tunable interatomic distances and detuning fields to satisfy perfect transport conditions.
result: Entanglement can be distributed at speeds approaching the quantum speed limit, with high fidelity under realistic parameters.
conclusion: Rydberg atom chains are a promising platform for fast entanglement distribution, relevant for quantum network nodes and quantum information processing.

title: Identifying Nonequilibrium Degrees Of Freedom In High-dimensional Stochastic Systems
authors: Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, And Gautam Reddy
abstract:
Author(s): Catherine Ji, Ravin Raj, Benjamin Eysenbach, and Gautam Reddy

Any coarse-grained description of a nonequilibrium system should faithfully represent its latent irreversible degrees of freedom. However, standard dimensionality reduction methods typically prioritize accurate reconstruction over physical relevance. Here, we introduce a model-free approach to ident…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023264] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A model-free method to identify latent irreversible degrees of freedom in high-dimensional stochastic systems.
motivation: Standard dimensionality reduction methods prioritize reconstruction over physical relevance, missing nonequilibrium degrees of freedom.
method: Introduces a data-driven approach based on the asymmetry of the covariance matrix of time-lagged increments to detect irreversible components.
result: Successfully identifies nonequilibrium degrees of freedom in simulated and real-world high-dimensional stochastic systems.
conclusion: The method provides a physically meaningful coarse-graining for nonequilibrium systems, relevant to stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Work Control For An Activity-driven Odd Tracer In A Viscoelastic Bath
authors: Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), And Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), and Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

We revisit the work-optimal driving of an effective odd tracer subject to active fluctuations, confined in a rotationally asymmetric harmonic trap and immersed in a viscoelastic (Maxwell) bath, using the standard protocol of translating the trap center. The odd mobility of an odd tracer need not be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023248] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal work protocols for an active odd tracer in a viscoelastic bath, focusing on thermodynamic efficiency and control.
motivation: Understanding work-optimal driving in active systems with odd mobility and viscoelastic memory is important for designing efficient nanoscale machines.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework based on a Langevin equation for an odd tracer in a Maxwell bath, and optimize the trap translation protocol to minimize work.
result: They derive conditions for optimal work and show that odd mobility and viscoelasticity significantly affect the optimal protocol and efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermodynamic control of active particles in complex environments, with potential applications in active matter and nanoscale thermodynamics.

title: Near-ultimate Quantum-enhanced Sensitivity In Dissipative Critical Sensing With Partial Access
authors: Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, and Victor Montenegro

Quantum sensors are powerful devices that exploit quantum effects to detect minute quantities with extremely high precision. Two obstacles to harnessing the full capacity of quantum probes are the resource-intensive preparation of the probe and the need for sophisticated measurements that typically …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023241] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that dissipative critical quantum sensors can achieve near-ultimate sensitivity even with partial access to the system, using a single quadrature measurement.
motivation: Quantum sensors face obstacles from resource-intensive probe preparation and sophisticated measurements; this work aims to overcome these by exploiting criticality in dissipative systems with simpler measurements.
method: The authors analyze a dissipative critical sensor near a phase transition, deriving the quantum Fisher information and showing that optimal scaling can be achieved by measuring only one quadrature of the output field.
result: They prove that the sensitivity scales as N^{-3/2} (Heisenberg scaling) with the number of probes N, even with partial access, and that this is near the ultimate quantum limit.
conclusion: Dissipative critical sensors with simple measurements can approach fundamental precision bounds, making them practical for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Compact Cavity-dressed Hamiltonian Framework At Arbitrarily Strong Light-matter Coupling
authors: Jakub Garwoła And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Jakub Garwoła and Dvira Segal

Researchers derive a nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized field modes and apply it to the open Rabi model and the Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model. They demonstrate advantage over conventional approaches in terms of error scaling with Hilbert space dimension and reveal cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically, achieving computational savings over brute-force simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022039] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized fields, applied to the Rabi and Dicke-Heisenberg models, with improved error scaling and computational savings.
motivation: Strong light-matter coupling regimes are challenging for conventional open quantum system methods; a more efficient and accurate framework is needed.
method: Derives a compact cavity-dressed Hamiltonian framework using a nonperturbative mapping that transforms the system into a dressed basis, enabling efficient simulation.
result: The method shows better error scaling with Hilbert space dimension compared to standard approaches, and reveals cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for simulating strongly coupled light-matter systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Measuring Temporal Entropies In Experiments
authors: Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, And Luca Tagliacozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, and Luca Tagliacozzo

We propose an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems. Our approach involves using local operators as probes to characterize the out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by a geometric double quench on a replicated system. Such protocol mimics the path…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023229] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems using local operators and a geometric double quench.
motivation: Temporal entropies are key to understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics and information scrambling, but experimental measurement has been challenging.
method: The protocol uses local operators as probes on a replicated system undergoing a geometric double quench, mimicking a path integral that yields temporal entropies.
result: The approach provides a feasible experimental scheme to extract temporal entropies, demonstrated with numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work bridges theory and experiment for measuring temporal entropies, enabling new insights into quantum dynamics and information flow.

title: Micromagnet-free Operation Of Electron Spin Qubits In $\mathrm{Si}/{\mathrm{Si}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{x}$ Vertical Double Quantum Dots
authors: Abhikbrata Sarkar And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Abhikbrata Sarkar and Daniel Loss

We study a vertical double quantum dot (DQD) in a [MATH] double-well heterostructure for full electrical control of electron Loss-DiVincenzo (LD) spin qubits, using realistic device modeling and numerical simulations. Due to the emerging spin-o…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023232] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a micromagnet-free design for electron spin qubits in Si/SiGe vertical double quantum dots using intrinsic spin-orbit coupling for full electrical control.
motivation: To eliminate the need for micromagnets in spin qubit devices, simplifying fabrication and reducing noise sources while maintaining full electrical control.
method: Realistic device modeling and numerical simulations of a vertical double quantum dot in a Si/SiGe heterostructure, exploiting spin-orbit coupling from the heterostructure interface.
result: Demonstrates that spin-orbit coupling enables fast and coherent qubit rotations without micromagnets, with gate fidelities comparable to conventional designs.
conclusion: Micromagnet-free operation is feasible and could simplify quantum dot qubit architectures, advancing scalability.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving insensitivity to common-mode noise.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a scalable, noise-robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states of spin ensembles that are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode phase shifts, and analyze their use in a differential phase sensing protocol.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states provide a quantum advantage in sensitivity while being robust to common-mode noise, enabling practical sensor networks.
conclusion: This work offers a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks by leveraging entanglement for noise-robust sensing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
