tldr: A trapped-ion experiment demonstrates generation of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are essential for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a bichromatic laser field to engineer a Hamiltonian that produces arbitrary superpositions of Fock states, leveraging the ion's internal qubit for control.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical nature via Wigner function tomography.
conclusion: The method provides a versatile platform for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, enabling advances in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms with high fidelity.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, revealing mechanisms that cause qubits to escape computational states.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing errors in superconducting qubit systems.
method: The authors use spectroscopic and time-resolved measurements to observe multiphoton resonances and characterize Landau-Zener transitions in transmon qubits.
result: They identify specific multiphoton processes that lead to ionization and quantify their rates, showing how these transitions depend on control parameters.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform the design of better readout and error mitigation strategies.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction even with advanced shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in superconducting qubit arrays exposed to environmental radiation.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array and model the effect of ionizing radiation on qubit coherence.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists despite state-of-the-art radiation protection, degrading error correction performance.
conclusion: Correlated phase errors from radiation pose a fundamental challenge for superconducting quantum processors, requiring novel mitigation strategies.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum circuits is crucial for quantum computing and statistical mechanics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in many-body chaotic quantum circuits.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition disappears in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the absence of a sharp Trotterization transition in large systems.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Complex open quantum systems are computationally expensive to simulate; a reduction method that preserves relevant dynamics for given measurement capabilities is needed.
method: The authors propose measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which integrates out fast degrees of freedom that are not resolved by the measurement apparatus, leading to an effective reduced model.
result: The technique is demonstrated on examples, showing accurate reproduction of measurement outcomes with significantly reduced computational cost.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems in contexts where only coarse-grained observations are available, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the Rydberg blockade mechanism.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The optimized multiqubit gates enable more efficient quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms, advancing the viability of these systems for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enhance photon blockade, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to achieve blockade with weaker coupling.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to stronger antibunching and higher transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic transitions but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions and computer algebra to optimize variational counterdiabatic driving, enabling more accurate suppression of transitions.
result: The new method achieves higher fidelity in quantum control compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving.
conclusion: This approach provides a readily available upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to identify Majorana bound states in interacting systems and assess their protection for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and measures of robustness and locality for Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, likely using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and characterize how interactions affect their non-Abelian properties.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to evaluate Majorana platforms, guiding experiments toward realizing robust topological qubits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods often scale poorly with system size or target only independent noise.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, enabling systematic cancellation of k-local correlated noise.
result: They produce device-tailored sequences whose length depends only on the noise order k, not the number of qubits, and demonstrate effectiveness on various noise models.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical, scalable noise mitigation for multi-qubit systems.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing bounds on loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory, deriving concentration bounds for the loss function based on circuit expressivity and noise strength.
result: They show that noise can reduce the effective dimension of the circuit's output distribution, leading to concentration of loss functions, and provide estimates for the variance of the loss under various noise models.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by balancing noise and expressivity, guiding the design of trainable variational circuits.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without adding noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This all-optical approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that combine deterministic and randomized Trotter steps, analyzing their error scaling and resource requirements for phase estimation.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude reduction in the number of Trotter steps needed for given accuracy, with rigorous bounds on the success probability and phase estimation error.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and provably efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, with immediate applications in quantum chemistry and beyond.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol for multilevel quantum systems that improves nondemolition measurement fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from back-action that destroys the quantum state. A nondemolition readout is crucial for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis based on prior outcomes, using a silicon quantum dot platform with spin qudits.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% with reduced measurement time and significantly lower measurement-induced errors compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a powerful technique for improving nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms and essential for scalable quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix, and characterize the critical noise threshold.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, using a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used to simulate variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation for near-term quantum computing.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors are a major obstacle for spin qubit quantum computing; suppressing them during idle periods is crucial for high-fidelity operations.
method: The authors tune the pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons in a triangular quantum dot to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally achieve a leakage-suppressed idle operation, demonstrating reduced error rates compared to standard operation.
conclusion: Equalizing exchange interactions provides a simple and effective method to protect spin qubits from leakage during idling, improving overall qubit performance.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems, which is a core interest in information thermodynamics.
method: The authors use repeated interventions to construct projected ensembles of process tensors, which encode the influence of an environment on a system, and analyze their properties to detect chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensemble approach can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics and provides a unified framework for various chaos diagnostics.
conclusion: This work offers a new tool for probing quantum chaos, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and the study of thermalization in many-body systems.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving parity dynamics for Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.
motivation: To realize Majorana-based qubits, fast and noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems is needed to resolve key processes and parity dynamics.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry to probe coupled quantum dot and superconductor devices, measuring the reflected signal to infer charge and parity states.
result: They demonstrate the ability to resolve parity dynamics and key processes in a minimal Kitaev chain device, showing the feasibility of this readout technique.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a promising readout method for Majorana-based qubits, enabling fast and noninvasive measurements essential for quantum information processing.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control via shared control lines incurs only logarithmic overhead, making it efficient for scaling quantum processors.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires many control lines, which is challenging. The authors investigate whether time-multiplexing (serializing control) can reduce hardware overhead without significant performance penalties.
method: They analyze the overhead of time-multiplexed control in terms of circuit depth and gate fidelity, considering different qubit topologies and gate configurations. They derive scaling laws for serialization costs.
result: The overhead scales only logarithmically with the number of qubits, and for certain two-qubit gate configurations, there is no overhead at all.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable strategy for scaling quantum processors, as the serialization cost is minimal and can be avoided in some cases.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and practical implementations.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer advantages in quantum communication, such as compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution, but require a unified overview of recent advances.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols, including CV-QKD, entanglement-based schemes, and quantum networks, discussing theoretical security proofs and experimental realizations.
result: CV quantum communication is now as mature as discrete-variable approaches, with demonstrated long-distance QKD, high secret key rates, and progress toward quantum repeaters and network architectures.
conclusion: CV techniques are a viable and promising platform for practical quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in loss, noise, and integration with quantum memories.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols that go beyond key distribution.
method: The paper reviews theoretical security definitions and limitations of various quantum crypto primitives, and discusses experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It categorizes quantum crypto primitives and explains their security guarantees and practical constraints.
conclusion: Quantum resources can enhance cryptography beyond QKD, but many protocols have significant theoretical limitations and experimental challenges.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification that can guide future experiments and theory in nonequilibrium quantum thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper surveys ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times (T2) for various solid-state spin qubits, including NV centers and SiV centers.
result: Cluster expansion techniques provide reliable predictions for T2 times in many cases, but challenges remain for systems where higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects dominate.
conclusion: Computational approaches are maturing and can guide the design of spin qubits with improved coherence, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories without assuming a specific quantum gravity framework.
method: The paper reviews theoretical proposals for tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes, analyzing their feasibility and implications.
result: Several feasible experimental setups are identified that could detect gravitationally induced entanglement, providing a test of the quantum nature of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with promising tabletop-scale experiments on the horizon.

title: Adaptable Route To Fast Coherent State Transport Via Bang-Bang-Bang Protocols
authors: Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, And H. H. Jen
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Tang Yu, Hsin-Lien Lee, Shao-Hung Chung, Ting Hsu, Guin-Dar Lin, Ying-Cheng Chen, and H. H. Jen

Fast coherent state transport is essential to quantum computation and quantum information processing. While an adiabatic transport of atomic qubits guarantees a high fidelity of the state preparation, it requires a long timescale that defies efficient quantum operations. Here, we propose an adaptabl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230802] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an adaptable bang-bang-bang protocol for fast coherent state transport of atomic qubits, achieving high fidelity with reduced time.
motivation: Adiabatic transport is slow, limiting efficient quantum operations; fast transport is needed for scalable quantum computation.
method: Uses a bang-bang-bang control sequence with three instantaneous pulses to steer the atomic state along a geodesic in Hilbert space, optimized via numerical search.
result: Demonstrates transport fidelities above 99.9% for timescales orders of magnitude shorter than adiabatic limits, with robustness to parameter variations.
conclusion: The protocol offers a practical, adaptable route for fast coherent transport in quantum information processing platforms like trapped ions or neutral atoms.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of high-fidelity ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with spin resolution.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity preparation of fermionic atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum simulation and computing.
method: Uses optical tweezers and spin-resolved imaging with large differential magnetic moments to prepare arbitrary two-component product states.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% in a 10×10 array.
conclusion: This platform enables scalable, high-fidelity fermionic quantum processors.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, leading to faster thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven quantum systems and how multi-frequency driving can circumvent that protection is important for controlling nonequilibrium phases.
method: The authors study a disordered spin chain under two-frequency periodic driving, analyzing heating rates and prethermal plateaus via numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the prethermal plateau that would exist under single-frequency driving, causing the system to heat more rapidly.
conclusion: Multi-frequency driving can overcome disorder-induced suppression of heating, which has implications for Floquet engineering and quantum control.

title: Global Versus Local Discrimination Of Locally Implementable Multipartite Unitaries
authors: Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, And Debashis Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Satyaki Manna, Sneha Suresh, Anandamay Das Bhowmik, and Debashis Saha

We study single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC) and global operations. As unitary discrimination depends on both the choice of probing states and the measurements on the evolved states, we classify LOCC…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062209] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the single-shot distinguishability of locally implementable multipartite unitaries under LOCC and global operations, classifying LOCC strategies and comparing their power to global operations.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of LOCC in discriminating quantum operations is fundamental for quantum information processing and communication.
method: The authors classify LOCC strategies for unitary discrimination and analyze the optimal success probability using different probing states and measurements.
result: They provide a classification of LOCC strategies and show that global operations can outperform LOCC in certain cases, with explicit examples.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum operation discrimination under locality constraints, with implications for quantum communication and computation.

title: Non-Markovianity-based Ultrasensitive Parameter Estimation
authors: Olli Siltanen
abstract:
Author(s): Olli Siltanen

Accurate parameter estimation is a central task in quantum metrology and sensing, where quantum resources can provide precision beyond classical limits. In realistic settings, however, system-environment interactions lead to decoherence, reducing these strategies to their classical counterparts. Noi…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062427] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that non-Markovianity can enhance the precision of parameter estimation in quantum metrology beyond the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard quantum metrology suffers from decoherence due to Markovian noise, which limits precision. Non-Markovian environments, which retain memory, may offer a resource to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors analyze a qubit probe coupled to a non-Markovian environment and derive the quantum Fisher information for parameter estimation, comparing it to the Markovian case.
result: Non-Markovianity leads to a scaling of precision that can surpass the standard quantum limit, with the enhancement depending on the memory time of the environment.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity is a useful resource for ultrasensitive parameter estimation, providing a new avenue for quantum metrology in realistic noisy settings.

title: Theory Of The Correlated Quantum Zeno Effect In A Monitored Qubit Dimer
authors: Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, And Alberto Biella
abstract:
Author(s): Severino Zeni, Gobinda Chakraborty, Alessandro Romito, and Alberto Biella

We theoretically investigate the stochastic dynamics of two qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements. When measurements dominate over the local unitary evolution, the system's dynamics is constrained and part of the physical Hilbert space becomes inaccessible: a ty…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062424] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the stochastic dynamics of two monitored qubits, revealing a correlated quantum Zeno effect that restricts the accessible Hilbert space and leads to a dissipative phase transition.
motivation: Understanding how continuous weak measurements affect the dynamics of quantum systems is crucial for quantum control and thermodynamics of monitored systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a dimer of qubits subject to one- and two-site correlated continuous weak measurements, using a stochastic master equation approach.
result: They find that when measurements dominate, the dynamics is constrained, leading to a correlated quantum Zeno effect and a dissipative phase transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the interplay between measurement and unitary evolution, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Chirped-pulse Engineering For Robust Control Of Single-molecule Orientation In A Cavity
authors: Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, And Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract:
Author(s): Li-Bao Fan, Yu Guo, Shan Ma, and Chuan-Cun Shu

We present a theoretical investigation of coherent control over the orientation of an individual molecule strongly coupled with a cavity using chirped-pulse driving. Specifically, we explore the dynamics of carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules under the influence of two chirped pulses with different spe…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063106] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates coherent control of single-molecule orientation in a cavity using chirped pulses, relevant to hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve robust orientation control of molecules strongly coupled to a cavity, which is important for quantum information processing and molecular-scale devices.
method: The authors model carbonyl sulfide (OCS) molecules in a cavity and apply two chirped pulses with different speeds to control molecular orientation, solving the quantum dynamics.
result: Chirped-pulse driving enables efficient and robust orientation control, with performance depending on pulse parameters and cavity coupling strength.
conclusion: Chirped-pulse engineering offers a promising approach for coherent control of molecular orientation in cavity QED, with potential applications in quantum technologies.

title: Fast Collisional $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ Gate For Fermionic Atoms In An Optical Superlattice
authors: Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, And Yoav Sagi
abstract:
Author(s): Rafi Weill, Jonathan Nemirovsky, and Yoav Sagi

Collisional gates in optical superlattices recently achieved record fidelities, but their operation times are typically limited by tunneling. Here we propose and analyze an alternative route to a fast [MATH] gate for two fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice based on optimized, …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063310] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a fast collisional √SWAP gate for fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice using optimized control.
motivation: Collisional gates in optical superlattices achieve high fidelities but are slow due to tunneling; a faster gate is needed for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors design and optimize a pulse sequence for a collisional √SWAP gate using fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice, leveraging controlled interactions and tunneling.
result: The proposed gate achieves operation times significantly shorter than typical tunneling-limited gates while maintaining high fidelity.
conclusion: The fast collisional gate enables faster quantum operations in optical superlattice platforms, advancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: On-demand Single-to-biphoton Conversion In An Atom-coupled Chiral Waveguide
authors: Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. la Rocca, And Jin-Hui Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Mao-Hua Wang, M. Artoni, G. C. La Rocca, and Jin-Hui Wu

On-demand generation of photon pairs is here achieved through non-standard waveguide QED, where a four-level atom is strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide. Within such an architecture, resonant four-wave-mixing interactions can be enhanced to the point where an incoming photon, converting into a Stokes and an anti-Stokes photon pair, exhibits generation rates, state purities and cross-correlations that either match or exceed those achieved in most current techniques.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061702] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: On-demand single-to-biphoton conversion via four-wave mixing in a chiral waveguide QED system.
motivation: Efficient on-demand generation of photon pairs is crucial for quantum networks and information processing.
method: A four-level atom strongly coupled to a chiral waveguide enables resonant four-wave mixing, converting an incoming photon into a Stokes-anti-Stokes pair.
result: The scheme achieves high generation rates, state purities, and cross-correlations comparable to or exceeding existing techniques.
conclusion: This chiral waveguide QED platform offers a promising route for deterministic photon-pair sources.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact quantum master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact master equations for multistate/multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Employs an equation-of-motion approach to obtain exact quantum master equations focusing on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model.
result: Successfully derives exact master equations for double-excitation dynamics, enabling accurate description of dissipative dynamics in this model.
conclusion: The approach offers a tractable way to handle complex multistate quantum systems, relevant for hybrid quantum systems involving cavity QED.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the Maximum Independent Set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The Maximum Independent Set problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embedding schemes require high atom overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to embed arbitrary graphs, leveraging the van der Waals interaction to encode the MIS constraint, and analyze the required number of atoms and interaction strengths.
result: The 3D embedding scheme reduces the atom overhead compared to 2D methods, enabling more efficient encoding of larger graphs.
conclusion: The proposed 3D embedding provides a practical improvement for implementing MIS problems on Rydberg atom quantum simulators, advancing the feasibility of quantum optimization on near-term hardware.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the detection loophole affects the performance of two entanglement detection criteria (PPT and moment-based) in a realistic measurement scenario.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that can compromise the reliability of detection methods.
method: The authors compare the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria under a detection loophole model, analyzing their detection probabilities and robustness using theoretical and numerical methods.
result: The PPT criterion, while more powerful in ideal setups, is more vulnerable to the detection loophole than moment-based criteria, which maintain better performance under realistic detector inefficiencies.
conclusion: Moment-based entanglement detection may be preferable in practical scenarios where detector inefficiencies are present, offering a trade-off between detection power and loophole resilience.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system via spontaneous four-wave mixing.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are crucial for quantum information protocols, but generating triphotons with high efficiency and purity remains challenging.
method: A six-level cold atomic system is used to produce energy-time-entangled triphotons through spontaneous four-wave mixing, leveraging electromagnetically induced transparency to enhance nonlinearity.
result: The scheme generates triphotons with high coincidence rates and strong energy-time entanglement, verified by correlation measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for generating multiphoton entanglement, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect In Subsystem Gauge Symmetry Restoration
authors: Hao-Yue Qi And Wei Zheng
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Yue Qi and Wei Zheng

Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge. Recently, the quantum Mpemba effect (QME)—a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon—has attracted considerable attention and has been extensively studied in systems with global symmetries. Here, we study the Q…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214311] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the quantum Mpemba effect in the context of subsystem gauge symmetry restoration, revealing a counterintuitive relaxation phenomenon in isolated quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in isolated quantum many-body systems is a central challenge, and the quantum Mpemba effect offers a novel perspective on non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors analyze the relaxation dynamics of a subsystem after a quench, focusing on the restoration of gauge symmetry and the emergence of the Mpemba effect using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the quantum Mpemba effect occurs in subsystem gauge symmetry restoration, with the relaxation rate depending on the initial state's symmetry properties.
conclusion: The work extends the study of the quantum Mpemba effect to systems with local symmetries, providing insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and relaxation processes.

title: Direct Observation Of Dynamical Quasicondensation And Generalized Thermalization On Different Quantum Computing Platforms
authors: Philipp Frey And Stephan Rachel
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Frey and Stephan Rachel

Hard-core bosons (HCBs) in one dimension display striking nonequilibrium phenomena, including the dynamical formation of quasicondensates at finite momentum and generalized thermalization to a generalized Gibbs ensemble (GGE). These effects, rooted in the integrability of the HCB model, have been ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224306] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper observes dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization of hard-core bosons on quantum computers, demonstrating non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To experimentally realize and study non-equilibrium phenomena like dynamical quasicondensation and generalized thermalization in a controlled quantum system.
method: The authors simulate hard-core bosons in one dimension on IBM and Quantinuum quantum processors, preparing initial states and measuring time evolution to observe quasicondensation and relaxation to a generalized Gibbs ensemble.
result: They directly observe the formation of finite-momentum quasicondensates and verify generalized thermalization via the generalized Gibbs ensemble, matching theoretical predictions.
conclusion: Quantum computing platforms can effectively simulate integrable many-body systems and reveal non-equilibrium thermodynamic behavior, validating theoretical models.

title: Limits Of The Lattice Bisognano-Wichmann Form For Entanglement Hamiltonians: A Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: Siyi Yang, Yi-Ming Ding, And Zheng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Siyi Yang, Yi-Ming Ding, and Zheng Yan

As a powerful theoretical construct, the entanglement Hamiltonian (EH) encapsulates the essential entanglement properties of a quantum many-body system. From the EH, one can extract a variety of entanglement quantities, such as entanglement entropies, negativity, and the entanglement spectrum. Howev…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235115] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum Monte Carlo to test the validity of the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form for entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: The entanglement Hamiltonian is a key tool for understanding quantum entanglement, but its exact form is often unknown; the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form is a proposed approximation whose limits need to be characterized.
method: The authors employ quantum Monte Carlo simulations to compute entanglement Hamiltonians for various lattice models and compare them to the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann prediction.
result: They find that the lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form accurately captures the entanglement Hamiltonian only in certain regimes, with deviations appearing for non-conformal or strongly interacting systems.
conclusion: The lattice Bisognano-Wichmann form has limited applicability, and alternative approaches are needed for generic quantum many-body systems.

title: Inverse Determination Of Light-matter Coupling In Disordered Systems From Transmittance Spectra
authors: Thales F. Macedo, Julián Faúndez, Antônio S. Coelho, Caio Lewenkopf, Mauro S. Ferreira, Felipe A. Pinheiro, And Natanael C. Costa
abstract:
Author(s): Thales F. Macedo, Julián Faúndez, Antônio S. Coelho, Caio Lewenkopf, Mauro S. Ferreira, Felipe A. Pinheiro, and Natanael C. Costa

We investigate quantum inverse problems in one-dimensional (1D) electronic disordered systems strongly coupled to optical cavities. More specifically, we consider the Anderson and the Aubry–André–Harper models connected to electronic reservoirs and embedded in a single-mode optical cavity. The light…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214202] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an inverse method to extract light-matter coupling parameters from transmittance spectra in disordered systems coupled to optical cavities.
motivation: Understanding light-matter coupling in disordered systems is crucial for cavity quantum electrodynamics and quantum simulation, but direct measurement is challenging.
method: The authors use machine learning to solve the inverse problem, training on simulated transmittance data from Anderson and Aubry-André-Harper models coupled to a single-mode cavity.
result: The method accurately retrieves coupling strengths and disorder parameters from transmittance spectra, even in the presence of noise.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for characterizing hybrid quantum systems, enabling experimental determination of key parameters in cavity-coupled disordered materials.

title: Making non-Markovian Master Equations Accessible With Approximate Environments
authors: Gerardo Suárez And Michał Horodecki
abstract:
Author(s): Gerardo Suárez and Michał Horodecki

Accurate and efficient simulation of open quantum systems remains a significant challenge, particularly for non-Markovian dynamics. We demonstrate the profound utility of expressing the environmental correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals within master equations. While not strictly requ…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064121] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to simplify non-Markovian master equations by approximating the environment correlation function as a sum of damped sinusoidals, making simulations more accessible.
motivation: Accurate simulation of open quantum systems with non-Markovian dynamics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a practical approximation that retains essential physics.
method: The environmental correlation function is expressed as a sum of damped sinusoidals, which allows the master equation to be cast in a form that is easier to solve numerically.
result: The approach yields accurate results for a range of non-Markovian scenarios while significantly reducing computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed approximation is a useful tool for studying open quantum systems, particularly in contexts where non-Markovian effects are important.

title: Multicriticality In Stochastic Dynamics Protected By Self-duality
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, and Juan P. Garrahan

In light of the recent interest in finding multicritical behavior in stochastic systems, we compute the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models (KCMs), demonstrating the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality. We further reveal that multic…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062101] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals multicritical behavior in the trajectory phase diagram of one-dimensional kinetically constrained models, protected by self-duality.
motivation: To find multicritical behavior in stochastic systems and understand dynamical phase transitions in kinetically constrained models.
method: The authors compute the trajectory phase diagram of 1D KCMs using self-duality and analyze the phase boundaries.
result: They demonstrate the existence of dynamical phases separated by lines of self-duality and uncover multicritical points.
conclusion: Self-duality protects multicriticality in stochastic dynamics, providing a framework for understanding dynamical phase transitions.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond via optical spectroscopy, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon interactions in color centers is crucial for improving coherence and performance in quantum networking and sensing applications.
method: Optical probing techniques, including linewidth analysis and coherent population trapping, are used to characterize the phononic environment of SnV centers.
result: The study reveals phonon-induced linewidth broadening and demonstrates coherent population trapping between ground-state orbital levels.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into phonon coupling in SnV centers, which can inform strategies to mitigate decoherence for quantum applications.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication requires accounting for relativistic effects due to high velocities and gravitational potentials, which can affect the security and performance of QKD.
method: The authors systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse Doppler, and gravitational redshift contributions, and model their impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how these shifts degrade the secret key rate and provide bounds for tolerable shifts, showing that compensation or inclusion in security analysis is necessary.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in satellite QKD to maintain security; the work provides a framework for modeling and mitigating these effects.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which is relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and showing convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: Achieves a unification of previously separate theories for diffusion and jump processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework can be applied to study thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, bridging discrete and continuous dynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular signaling may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multiphase coexistence, and non-equilibrium thermodynamics to model how condensates could classify and respond to signals.
result: They argue that phase transitions enable analog computation, signal integration, and memory in a way that is robust and efficient, with potential parallels to neural networks.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a new paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for synthetic biology and understanding of living systems.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints and the need for efficient dilation methods.
method: The paper introduces a dilation approach that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice as an ancillary system, employing moment-matching to approximate the target nonunitary evolution with a unitary circuit.
result: The method achieves near-optimal query complexity and circuit depth for simulating linear differential equations, overcoming traditional connectivity bottlenecks.
conclusion: This framework provides a practical and efficient way to simulate nonunitary processes on near-term quantum devices, with applications in quantum simulation and linear algebra.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle with intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method on a qubit platform, extracting noise cross-correlations and revealing new features of the noise environment.
conclusion: This technique provides a powerful tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits and better quantum error correction.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal error correction architecture for neutral-atom quantum simulators, enabling megaquop-scale simulations with reduced logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at scale requires fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing error correction schemes impose high space and time overhead. The authors aim to design a more efficient architecture tailored to neutral-atom hardware.
method: They integrate a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction scheme with neutral-atom hardware and extend it to high-rate codes, optimizing logical layout and resource usage.
result: The proposed architecture yields significant savings in logical qubit count, physical qubit count, and runtime for quantum simulation tasks, bringing megaquop-scale simulations closer to feasibility.
conclusion: The transversal architecture demonstrates a practical path toward large-scale quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, highlighting the importance of hardware-software co-design.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics in confining systems.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in quantum systems is important for probing confinement and non-equilibrium dynamics, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and simulation.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and experimental demonstrations with trapped ions to study string-breaking dynamics under adiabatic and diabatic conditions.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits complex quantum dynamics beyond simple breaking, including oscillatory and multi-particle effects.
conclusion: The work provides new probes of string breaking and demonstrates that confining strings can show rich quantum dynamics, relevant for quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
