Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes using code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially for protecting quantum memories during computation.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without requiring additional code blocks, preserving key code properties and enabling more efficient quantum computation.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a method for parallel logical measurements on LDPC codes, which is essential for scalable architectures.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Implements a trapped-ion quantum processor with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to execute a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies.
result: Achieves accurate molecular energy estimates with error mitigation and partial fault tolerance, demonstrating a path toward practical quantum chemistry on noisy devices.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically combined with variational algorithms to improve the accuracy of molecular simulations, advancing the feasibility of quantum computing for chemistry.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to tune the oscillator's asymmetry, enabling simulation of chemical activation processes.
conclusion: This work shows that parametric oscillators can serve as quantum simulators for chemical dynamics, bridging quantum optics and quantum chemistry.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium review that provides a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them. This review aims to unify approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, and provides guidance on choosing appropriate techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: A unified perspective helps bridge gaps between communities and facilitates progress in simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate complexity and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce gate counts and simplify certain operations, potentially improving efficiency and scalability.
method: The paper surveys qudit-based decompositions of multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), qudit-qubit embeddings, and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of some multiqubit gates, reducing the number of operations and physical resources needed, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing gate complexity, but challenges remain in qudit control and error correction.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between local and global quantum resources is fundamental for quantum information processing. This work aims to experimentally verify a theoretical bound on the sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information.
method: The authors prepare two-qubit states using a photonic platform and measure local coherence via quantum state tomography and quantum mutual information via correlation measurements. They vary the state parameters to explore the trade-off.
result: They observe that the sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit, confirming the predicted complementarity relation.
conclusion: The results provide experimental evidence for a fundamental trade-off between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum resource theories and quantum information protocols.

title: Minimum Uncertainty States And Squeezed States From A Sum Uncertainty Relation
authors: Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, And Namrata Shukla
abstract:
Author(s): Yatindra Kumar, Yashraj Jha, and Namrata Shukla

Heisenberg's uncertainty relation is at the origin of understanding minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states of light. In the recent past, the sum uncertainty relation was formulated by Maccone and Pati [L. Maccone and A. K. Pati,
tldr: The paper derives minimum uncertainty states and squeezed states from a sum uncertainty relation, extending the concept beyond the standard Heisenberg-Robertson relation.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for minimum uncertainty and squeezed states using a stronger sum uncertainty relation, which may offer new insights into quantum states.
method: The authors use the sum uncertainty relation by Maccone and Pati to derive conditions for minimum uncertainty states and identify squeezed states that satisfy these conditions.
result: They find that the sum uncertainty relation yields a broader class of minimum uncertainty states, including some that are not captured by the standard product uncertainty relation.
conclusion: The sum uncertainty relation provides a more comprehensive characterization of minimum uncertainty and squeezed states, potentially useful for quantum optics and information.

title: Optimizing Fault-tolerant Cat State Preparation
authors: Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, And Robert Wille
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Peham, Erik Weilandt, and Robert Wille

Cat states are an important resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, where they serve as building blocks for a variety of fault-tolerant primitives. Consequently, the ability to prepare high-quality cat states at large fault distances is essential. While optimizations for low fault distances o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062426] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents optimizations for fault-tolerant cat state preparation, focusing on reducing resource overhead for large fault distances.
motivation: Cat states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but preparing them at large fault distances is resource-intensive. Existing optimizations for low distances do not scale well.
method: The authors propose a method to optimize the preparation of cat states by reducing the number of required qubits and gates, using a combination of stabilizer formalism and circuit synthesis techniques.
result: They demonstrate significant reductions in qubit count and gate depth for cat states at various fault distances, with improvements over previous methods.
conclusion: The optimized cat state preparation enables more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing, particularly for large-scale implementations.

title: Decoherence Across Phase-space Scales: From Compass States To General Quantum States
authors: Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Naeem Akhtar, Jia-Xin Peng, Tan Hailin, Xiaosen Yang, and Dong Wang

Environmental decoherence occurs when a quantum system interacts with its surroundings, progressively reducing quantum interference and coherence, complicating the preservation of critical quantum features over time, especially during experimental implementation. The quantum features of a state can …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062421] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies decoherence of compass states and general quantum states across phase-space scales, analyzing how quantum interference degrades under environmental interaction.
motivation: Understanding decoherence is crucial for preserving quantum features in experiments, but the effect across different phase-space scales is not well characterized.
method: The authors use phase-space methods (e.g., Wigner function) to quantify decoherence for compass states and extend the analysis to general quantum states, examining how coherence decays at different scales.
result: They find that decoherence rates depend on the phase-space scale, with fine-scale features decaying faster, and provide a general framework for predicting decoherence dynamics.
conclusion: The work offers insights into decoherence mechanisms that can inform strategies for protecting quantum coherence in practical implementations.

title: Globalized Critical Quantum Metrology In The Dynamics Of The Quantum Rabi Model By An Auxiliary Nonlinear Term
authors: Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, And Zu-Jian Ying
abstract:
Author(s): Qiu-Yi Chen, Feng Qiao, and Zu-Jian Ying

The quantum Rabi model (QRM) is a fundamental model for light-matter interactions; the finite-component quantum phase transition (QPT) in the QRM has established a paradigmatic application for critical quantum metrology (CQM). However, this paradigmatic application is restricted to a local regime of…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062423] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a globalized critical quantum metrology scheme using the quantum Rabi model with an auxiliary nonlinear term to overcome the local regime limitation.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology in the quantum Rabi model is limited to a local regime; the authors aim to extend it to a global regime by introducing a nonlinear term.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of the quantum Rabi model with an added nonlinear term, studying the quantum phase transition and its impact on metrological sensitivity.
result: The auxiliary nonlinear term enables globalized critical quantum metrology, enhancing sensitivity beyond the local regime.
conclusion: The proposed scheme broadens the applicability of critical quantum metrology in light-matter interaction models.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hyperentanglement-based quantum reservoir computing framework that uses multiple degrees of freedom of photons to enhance computational performance.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is promising for temporal tasks, but standard QRC with single-degree-of-freedom entanglement may be limited. Hyperentanglement offers richer resources for improved performance.
method: The authors design a QRC architecture where hyperentangled photons (entangled in polarization and orbital angular momentum) serve as the reservoir, with input encoding and output readout via linear optics and measurements.
result: Numerical simulations show that hyperentanglement-based QRC outperforms classical reservoirs and standard QRC on benchmark tasks like time-series prediction and classification, with higher accuracy and faster convergence.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement provides a viable resource for enhancing quantum reservoir computing, potentially leading to more powerful quantum machine learning systems.

title: Solovay-Kitaev Algorithm And Randomized Compilation
authors: Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. Mcfarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, And Peter J. Love
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. McFarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, and Peter J. Love

We analyze the use of the Solovay-Kitaev (SK) algorithm to generate an ensemble of one-qubit rotations over which to perform randomized compilation. We perform simulations to compare the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit [MATH] rotation and discrete SK dec…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062418] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for generating one-qubit rotation ensembles used in randomized compilation, comparing trace distances between ideal and discretized rotations.
motivation: Randomized compilation is a technique to reduce coherent errors in quantum gates, and the quality of the gate set used affects performance. The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm provides a way to approximate arbitrary single-qubit gates with a finite universal gate set, but its impact on randomized compilation has not been thoroughly studied.
method: The authors simulate the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm to generate ensembles of one-qubit rotations and compute the trace distance between the ideal quantum state and the state obtained after applying the discretized rotation from the SK decomposition.
result: The simulations show that the trace distance decreases as the SK recursion depth increases, and they characterize the distribution of distances for different target rotations.
conclusion: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm can effectively generate high-quality gate sets for randomized compilation, but the overhead in gate count may be significant; the paper provides quantitative guidance for choosing SK parameters.

title: Attributed-graph Kernel Implementation Using Local Detuning Of A Neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian
authors: Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, And Shaheen Acheche
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, and Shaheen Acheche

We extend the quantum-feature kernel framework, which relies on measurements of graph-dependent observables, along three directions. First, leveraging neutral-atom quantum processing units, we introduce a scheme that incorporates attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062608] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum-feature kernel methods to attributed graphs using neutral-atom Rydberg systems, with experimental implementation on a quantum processing unit.
motivation: To enable graph classification with attributed graphs (edge features) on quantum hardware, leveraging the native capabilities of neutral-atom Rydberg arrays.
method: The authors embed edge features into atomic positions and use local detuning of the Rydberg Hamiltonian to encode graph structure, then measure observables to compute kernel values.
result: They demonstrate the scheme on a neutral-atom quantum processor, showing that attributed graph kernels can be implemented with high fidelity and scalability.
conclusion: The work provides a practical pathway for quantum machine learning on attributed graphs, but the contribution is primarily algorithmic and experimental rather than advancing fundamental quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Corner Contribution To The Entanglement In Two-dimensional Systems: A Tensor Network Perspective
authors: Noa Feldman And Moshe Goldstein
abstract:
Author(s): Noa Feldman and Moshe Goldstein

In continuous quantum field theories, the entanglement entropy of a subsystem with sharp corners on its boundary exhibits a universal corner-dependent contribution. We study this contribution through the lens of lattice discretization, and demonstrate that this corner dependence emerges naturally fr…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224307] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the corner contribution to entanglement entropy in 2D systems using tensor networks, showing that lattice discretization naturally reproduces universal corner terms.
motivation: Understanding universal features of entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, particularly corner contributions, is important for characterizing quantum phases.
method: The authors use tensor network methods (likely matrix product states or projected entangled pair states) to compute entanglement entropy on lattices with sharp corners.
result: They demonstrate that the corner contribution to entanglement entropy emerges naturally from lattice discretization and matches field theory predictions.
conclusion: Tensor network approaches can capture universal corner contributions, providing a bridge between lattice models and continuum field theories.

title: Hydrodynamic Fluctuations Of Stochastic Charged Cellular Automata
authors: Takato Yoshimura And Žiga Krajnik
abstract:
Author(s): Takato Yoshimura and Žiga Krajnik

We study charge fluctuations of a family of stochastic charged cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit and obtain the exact typical charge probability distributions, known to be anomalous, using hydrodynamics. The cellular automata considered are examples of linearly degenera…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064120] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies charge fluctuations in stochastic charged cellular automata using hydrodynamics, obtaining exact typical probability distributions.
motivation: To understand anomalous charge fluctuations in stochastic cellular automata away from the deterministic single-file limit.
method: Hydrodynamic theory is applied to derive exact typical charge probability distributions for a family of stochastic charged cellular automata.
result: The exact typical charge probability distributions are obtained, which are anomalous.
conclusion: Hydrodynamics can successfully describe charge fluctuations in these stochastic systems, providing insight into non-equilibrium behavior.

title: Ergodicity And Hydrodynamics: From Quantum To Classical Spin Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, And Leonardo Mazza
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, and Leonardo Mazza

We show that in classical spin systems, the precise nature of the late-time hydrodynamic tails of the autocorrelation functions of a generic observable is determined by (i) the dynamical critical exponent and (ii) the equilibrium thermodynamic properties of the corresponding observable. We provide n…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064102] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that hydrodynamic tails in classical spin systems are determined by dynamical critical exponent and equilibrium thermodynamic properties, with a quantum extension.
motivation: Understanding late-time dynamics and hydrodynamic behavior in spin systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive analytic expressions for autocorrelation functions using hydrodynamic theory and test them with numerical simulations on classical and quantum spin chains.
result: They find that the late-time tails are governed by the dynamical critical exponent and the static susceptibility of the observable, and extend the result to quantum systems via the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for hydrodynamic tails in classical and quantum spin systems, linking dynamics to equilibrium properties.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize generation of non-Gaussian quantum states, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to improve success rates through systematic optimization.
method: The authors propose new control parameters beyond the stellar rank to characterize and optimize non-Gaussian state generation in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in success probability for generating target non-Gaussian states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for scalable generation of non-Gaussian optical states, advancing quantum information applications.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems, particularly in fractional quantum Hall states, is crucial for characterizing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: The authors perform entropy measurements in a partially filled Landau level using a graphene-based device, tracking entropy as a function of temperature and magnetic field.
result: They observe successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, and achieve sensitivity that constrains the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.
conclusion: The entropy measurements provide insights into the thermodynamics of strongly correlated electrons and may help identify topological order, but the paper is primarily experimental condensed matter physics without a strong information-theoretic or thermodynamic framework.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation is needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of QLDPC codes with high encoding rate and constant-depth encoding circuits, enabling fault-tolerant magic state distillation.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes achieve high thresholds and low overhead for magic state generation compared to existing schemes.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path to reduce the resource cost of magic states in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for surpassing classical limits in sensing.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including scaling of quantum Fisher information near critical points.
result: Demonstrates how criticality can be exploited to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling in parameter estimation.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing provides a promising route for high-precision metrology, but practical challenges remain.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations.
method: Applies Fourier neural operators to learn the Floquet Hamiltonian and predict observable dynamics and operator growth from training data.
result: The method accurately extrapolates dynamics beyond the training time window and captures operator growth features.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators are effective for learning and predicting the behavior of time-periodic quantum systems.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: They develop a technique to propagate errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of classical simulation for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The method achieves efficient classical simulation, enabling the analysis of larger and more complex magic state preparation protocols than previously possible.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for evaluating magic state preparation protocols, which is important for resource estimation in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieves single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths than previous single-shot codes.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds needed.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops fault-tolerant protocols for Majorana-based quantum codes, including gates, measurements, and high-rate code constructions.
motivation: To enable fault-tolerant quantum computation using fermionic systems, which require tailored error correction and logical operations beyond standard qubit approaches.
method: Generalizes qubit error correction and fault-tolerant techniques to fermionic processes, designing specific gates, measurements, and code families for Majorana-based platforms.
result: Presents fault-tolerant protocols and high-rate quantum codes suitable for Majorana-based qubits, demonstrating feasibility of universal quantum computation.
conclusion: Majorana-based quantum codes can support fault-tolerant operations, advancing the prospects for topological quantum computing.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to compress multimode photonic processors by identifying the most squeezed supermodes, reducing hardware scaling from quadratic to near-constant.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware with mode count, limiting scalability. The authors aim to reduce this overhead by exploiting the structure of squeezed light.
method: They propose a variational approach to find the most strongly squeezed supermodes in a multimode squeezed light source, then use only those modes for processing, effectively compressing the required hardware.
result: The method achieves near-constant hardware footprint regardless of the number of modes, dramatically reducing resource requirements for quantum information processing tasks.
conclusion: Variational identification of squeezed supermodes enables scalable multimode photonic quantum processors, with potential applications in quantum computing and sensing.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but diverse methods exist; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic methods (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: They show how these methods unify various approaches and provide tools for analyzing fluctuations and correlations.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful, unified framework for stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability beyond chemistry.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurement.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many materials exhibit properties that seem to exceed these bounds, prompting a need to understand the underlying assumptions and how they can be circumvented.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of materials and phenomena where measured properties exceed classical bounds, analyzing which assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linear response, homogeneity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies that apparent violations occur when measurements are made under conditions that violate the assumptions of the bounds, such as non-equilibrium, nonlinear, or heterogeneous systems.
conclusion: Understanding these violations can guide the design of materials with enhanced properties, but the findings are more about materials science than fundamental thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Dressed Bound States And non-Markovian Dynamics With A Whispering-gallery-mode Microcavity Coupled To A Two-level Atom And A Semi-infinite Photonic Waveguide
authors: J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, And H. Z. Shen
abstract:
Author(s): J. Y. Sun, C. Cui, Y. F. Li, Shuang Xu, Cheng Shang, Yan-Hui Zhou, and H. Z. Shen

We investigate dressed bound states in an open cavity with a whispering-gallery-mode microring coupled to a two-level atom and a waveguide with a mirror at the right end. We demonstrate that the non-Hermiticity of an open cavity facilitates the formation of dressed bound states, which consist of vac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063713] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dressed bound states and non-Markovian dynamics in an open cavity system coupled to a waveguide, focusing on the role of non-Hermiticity.
motivation: Understanding bound states in open quantum systems is important for controlling light-matter interactions and quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a whispering-gallery-mode microcavity coupled to a two-level atom and a semi-infinite waveguide with a mirror, using non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and master equation approaches.
result: They show that non-Hermiticity enables the formation of dressed bound states, which suppress spontaneous emission and lead to non-Markovian dynamics.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into engineering bound states in open systems, with potential applications in quantum memory and quantum networks.

title: Two-point Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Gradients In The Frequency Domain
authors: Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, And Hong-Fu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyang Song, Wei Zhang, Ji Cao, Xuexi Yi, and Hong-Fu Wang

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a leading platform for combinatorial optimization in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era. A central challenge for QAOA and related variational algorithms is how to obtain efficient, provably reliable gradient estimators. We develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062425] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a frequency-domain analysis of QAOA gradients to improve gradient estimation for variational quantum algorithms.
motivation: Efficient and reliable gradient estimation is a central challenge for QAOA and variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ era.
method: The authors analyze QAOA gradients in the frequency domain, deriving expressions that relate gradient components to the Fourier spectrum of the cost function.
result: They show that gradient estimation can be improved by exploiting the frequency structure, potentially reducing the number of required quantum measurements.
conclusion: The frequency-domain perspective offers a new approach to gradient estimation for QAOA, with implications for variational quantum algorithm optimization.

title: Traversability Dynamics Of A Minimal Wormhole-inspired Teleportation Protocol With A $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Deformation
authors: Sudhanva Joshi And Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Sudhanva Joshi and Sunil Kumar Mishra

Holography-inspired teleportation has recently emerged as a significant area of research in quantum many-body systems. In this work, we investigate the effects of [MATH]-symmetric nonunitary deformations on the traversability of the wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol modeled by coupled…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol with PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformations, focusing on traversability dynamics.
motivation: To understand how non-unitary deformations affect the traversability of holography-inspired teleportation in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors model the protocol as coupled qubits with PT-symmetric non-Hermitian terms and analyze the dynamics using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that PT-symmetric deformations can enhance or suppress traversability depending on parameters, and identify optimal regimes for teleportation fidelity.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian deformations offer a new control knob for quantum teleportation protocols inspired by wormhole physics, with potential implications for quantum information processing.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Unruh effect affects the precision of estimating Gaussian channel parameters using quantum metrology.
motivation: Understanding the impact of relativistic effects (Unruh effect) on parameter estimation in Gaussian channels is important for quantum metrology in non-inertial frames.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Fisher information for Gaussian channels under the influence of the Unruh effect, considering both single-mode and two-mode squeezed states.
result: The Unruh effect degrades the estimation precision, but using two-mode squeezed states can partially mitigate the loss.
conclusion: Relativistic motion imposes fundamental limits on quantum metrology, and optimal state preparation can improve precision.

title: Dichotomy Theorem Separating Complete Integrability And Nonintegrability Of Isotropic Spin Chains
authors: Naoto Shiraishi And Mizuki Yamaguchi
abstract:
Author(s): Naoto Shiraishi and Mizuki Yamaguchi

The authors prove here a long-anticipated dichotomy for general isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chains, stating that any model falls into one of two extremes – either having an infinite family of local conserved quantities (completely integrable), or admitting no nontrivial local conserved quantity (nonintegrable). This rules out intermediate models with only finitely many local conserved quantities. The authors also provide a simple criterion for deciding which case holds, greatly reducing the work needed to diagnose integrability.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241111] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proves a dichotomy for isotropic spin chains: either completely integrable with infinite local conserved quantities or nonintegrable with none, ruling out intermediate cases.
motivation: Understanding integrability in quantum many-body systems is crucial for thermalization and quantum chaos, but a complete classification for isotropic spin chains was missing.
method: The authors develop a rigorous mathematical proof using algebraic and combinatorial arguments to show that any isotropic nearest-neighbor spin chain either has an infinite family of local conserved quantities or none at all.
result: A dichotomy theorem is established, along with a simple criterion to determine which case holds, eliminating the possibility of models with finitely many local conserved quantities.
conclusion: This work provides a definitive classification of integrability in isotropic spin chains, with implications for understanding thermalization and non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Geometric Approach To Strongly Correlated Bosons: From $N$-representability To The Generalized Bose-Einstein Condensate Force
authors: Chih-Chun Wang And Christian Schilling
abstract:
Author(s): Chih-Chun Wang and Christian Schilling

Building on recent advances in reduced density matrix theory, we develop a geometric framework for describing strongly correlated lattice bosons. We first establish that translational symmetry, together with a fixed pair interaction, enables an exact functional formulation expressed solely in terms …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224511] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A geometric framework for strongly correlated bosons using reduced density matrix theory and N-representability conditions.
motivation: To develop an exact functional formulation for strongly correlated lattice bosons beyond mean-field approaches.
method: Leverages translational symmetry and fixed pair interactions to derive a geometric description based on reduced density matrices.
result: Establishes a generalized Bose-Einstein condensate force and provides insights into bosonic N-representability.
conclusion: The geometric approach offers a new perspective on strongly correlated bosons but is primarily a theoretical framework without direct quantum information or thermodynamics applications.

title: Unified Statistical Theory Of Heat Conduction In Nonuniform Media
authors: Yi Zeng And Jianjun Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Zeng and Jianjun Dong

Using the Zwanzig projection-operator formalism, we derive a causal two-point spatiotemporal kernel for heat conduction, defined microscopically as a space-resolved equilibrium heat-flux time-correlation function, that encodes temporal memory, spatial nonlocality, and material heterogeneity on equal…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235204] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Derives a causal two-point spatiotemporal kernel for heat conduction from microscopic equilibrium correlations using the Zwanzig projection-operator formalism.
motivation: To unify temporal memory, spatial nonlocality, and material heterogeneity in heat conduction within a single statistical framework.
method: Uses the Zwanzig projection-operator formalism to derive a space-resolved equilibrium heat-flux time-correlation function as the kernel.
result: Obtains a causal two-point spatiotemporal kernel that encodes memory, nonlocality, and heterogeneity on equal footing.
conclusion: Provides a unified statistical theory of heat conduction applicable to nonuniform media.

title: Boundary-induced Drift And Negative Mobility In Constrained Stochastic Systems
authors: Meitar Goldfarb And Stanislav Burov
abstract:
Author(s): Meitar Goldfarb and Stanislav Burov

We study overdamped stochastic dynamics confined by hard reflecting boundaries and show that the combination of boundary geometry and an anisotropic diffusion tensor generically generates directed motion. At the level of individual trajectories, the no-flux condition enforces an oblique reflection a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064119] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: Boundary geometry combined with anisotropic diffusion induces directed motion and negative mobility in overdamped stochastic systems.
motivation: To understand how hard reflecting boundaries and anisotropic diffusion can generate directed motion without external bias, and to explore the phenomenon of negative mobility.
method: Analytical and numerical study of overdamped Langevin dynamics with reflecting boundaries and anisotropic diffusion tensor, analyzing the no-flux condition and oblique reflection.
result: Boundary geometry generically produces directed drift; negative mobility (motion opposite to a weak force) emerges in certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: Boundary-induced drift is a generic mechanism for directed transport in confined stochastic systems, with potential implications for nanoscale devices and biological transport.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from d-dimensional cellular automata trajectories and studies their quantum phase transition.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, enabling the study of quantum phase transitions in the resulting models.
method: Uses the trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to define interactions in a (d+1)-dimensional classical spin model, then adds a transverse field to study the quantum phase transition.
result: Characterizes the quantum phase transition for all 256 elementary cellular automata rules, showing that the critical properties depend on the rule class.
conclusion: The construction provides a new family of quantum spin models with tunable critical behavior, linking cellular automata to statistical mechanics.

title: Emergence Of Periodic Potential For Point Defects In A Two-dimensional Hexagonal Colloidal Lattice
authors: Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, And Ping Ao
abstract:
Author(s): Xicheng Huang, Zefei Liu, Yong-Cong Chen, Guohong Yang, and Ping Ao

We examined the Brownian motion of point defects in a two-dimensional hexagonal colloidal crystal, going beyond the conventional treatment that assumes constant diffusion coefficients. By extracting the spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix directly from experimental trajectories, we u…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Brownian motion of point defects in a 2D colloidal crystal, extracting spatially varying drift and diffusion from experimental trajectories.
motivation: To go beyond constant diffusion coefficients and understand defect dynamics in a periodic potential landscape.
method: Experimental trajectories of point defects in a hexagonal colloidal lattice are analyzed to extract spatially varying drift vector and diffusion matrix.
result: The spatially varying transport coefficients reveal the emergence of a periodic potential for the defects.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed characterization of defect motion in a colloidal crystal, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, finding violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium phase transitions and test the validity of local equilibrium assumptions in systems with long-range interactions.
method: Numerical simulation of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives to reproduce low-wave-number density of states.
result: The system exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions.
conclusion: Fractional derivative models can capture nonequilibrium effects that challenge standard thermodynamic descriptions.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Yoshii and Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. When such a soliton state is coupled to a metallic substrate, local Coulomb interactions can give rise to Kondo screening. Here, we demons…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023243] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, showing that the Kondo scale can be controlled by the topological mass.
motivation: To understand correlation effects in topological systems and how topological bound states can host Kondo physics.
method: The authors use numerical methods (likely DMRG or exact diagonalization) to study an SSH chain with a magnetic impurity coupled to a metallic substrate.
result: They demonstrate that the Kondo temperature can be tuned by the topological mass parameter of the SSH chain.
conclusion: Topological bound states provide a controllable platform for Kondo physics, with potential applications in quantum simulation.

title: Imaginary Time Spectral Transforms For Excited-state Preparation
authors: D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, And S. J. Thomson
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, and S. J. Thomson

A variational method is presented for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems, combining a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion. Results are demonstrated for disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations within a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method combining shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to prepare excited states of many-body quantum systems.
motivation: Preparing excited eigenstates is important for understanding quantum systems, but existing methods are often computationally expensive or require matrix inversion.
method: The method uses a shift-invert spectral transformation to map excited states to ground states of a modified Hamiltonian, then applies imaginary time evolution via tensor networks, avoiding explicit matrix inversion.
result: The method is demonstrated on disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations, showing accurate preparation of excited states.
conclusion: The approach is compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations and offers a practical way to access excited states in many-body systems.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:

tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins at high magnetic field.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and device physics, but the paper focuses on a specific condensed matter system without direct connection to information-theoretic thermodynamics.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron and nuclear spin temperatures in mesoscopic metallic islands under high magnetic fields.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins.
conclusion: The work provides insights into heat flow and thermalization in mesoscopic systems, but is not directly relevant to the core interests in quantum information thermodynamics or computing.

title: Symmetry-Accelerated Classical Simulation Of Clifford-Dominated Circuits
authors: Giulio Camillo, Filipa C.R. Peres, Markus Heinrich, And Juani Bermejo-Vega
abstract:

Strong and weak symmetry reductions render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries beyond previous limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020356] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents symmetry-accelerated classical simulation of Clifford-dominated circuits using optimal stabilizer decompositions.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is important for benchmarking and understanding quantum advantage; Clifford-dominated circuits are classically simulable but require efficient methods.
method: The authors exploit strong and weak symmetry reductions to render optimal stabilizer decompositions tractable for multiqubit unitaries.
result: They achieve efficient classical simulation of circuits that are dominated by Clifford gates but include non-Clifford gates, extending the reach of classical simulation.
conclusion: Symmetry reduction enables practical classical simulation of larger Clifford-dominated circuits, which is relevant for verifying near-term quantum devices.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation

abstract:

[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum circuits.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for products of Pauli operators and use it to simplify circuits in the sequential Pauli-based computation model.
result: The proposed relation enables significant reduction in the number of T gates required for certain quantum circuits.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

motivation: Efficient spectral analysis of large matrices is important for quantum many-body systems, but worst-case complexity is high.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to identify clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral properties.
conclusion: The work provides a quantum algorithm for spectral analysis, but its connection to core quantum information topics is indirect.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for benchmarking and for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: The authors develop a Pauli propagation technique that tracks the evolution of Pauli operators under noisy quantum circuits, enabling efficient classical simulation.
result: They prove that for any local noise channel, the output distribution of a quantum circuit can be approximated classically in polynomial time, with the noise strength determining the approximation error.
conclusion: Arbitrary local noise renders typical quantum circuits classically simulable, highlighting the fragility of quantum computational advantage in noisy settings.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems for novel material properties.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory and pump-probe spectroscopy.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful route to engineer quantum states in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity effects and entanglement mediation.
motivation: Classical gravity is poorly tested at small scales; massive quantum systems may reveal quantum aspects of gravity.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and entanglement generation.
result: Summarizes current understanding and experimental progress on gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems are promising for testing quantum gravity, but no definitive results yet.

title: Detuning The Floquet Anomalous Chiral Spin Liquid
authors: Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, And Didier Poilblanc
abstract:
Author(s): Matthieu Mambrini, Nathan Goldman, and Didier Poilblanc

At high frequency, a periodically driven quantum spin-1/2 system can emulate a chiral spin liquid (CSL) described by an effective static local chiral Hamiltonian. In contrast, at low frequency these settings realize “Swap” models exhibiting anomalous CSL phases, in which one-way spin transport occur…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224423] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a periodically driven spin system that exhibits an anomalous chiral spin liquid phase with one-way spin transport, focusing on the effect of detuning the driving frequency.
motivation: To understand how detuning from the high-frequency regime affects the stability and properties of Floquet-induced chiral spin liquids, which are of interest for topological phases and spin transport.
method: The authors use numerical simulations (likely exact diagonalization or tensor networks) to analyze the effective Hamiltonian and spin dynamics of a driven spin-1/2 system as a function of driving frequency.
result: They find that at low frequencies, the system realizes 'Swap' models with anomalous CSL phases exhibiting one-way spin transport, and detuning modifies the phase diagram and transport properties.
conclusion: Detuning the driving frequency can be used to control the chiral spin liquid phase and its transport characteristics, offering a tunable platform for studying topological order.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are a new class of LDPC codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decoding for fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory requires error-correcting codes with high thresholds and low overhead, but existing codes often have trade-offs between these properties.
method: The authors introduce radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes with tunable parameters, and analyze their performance using numerical simulations and analytical bounds.
result: Radial codes achieve high error thresholds, low qubit overhead, and support single-shot error correction, making them promising for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for practical fault-tolerant quantum memory, balancing threshold, overhead, and decoding complexity.

title: Observation Of Five Distinct Localization Phases In A 1d Floquet System

motivation: To experimentally realize and characterize critical phases in disordered Floquet systems, which are less explored than extended and localized phases.
method: Using a 1D Floquet system with controlled disorder and driving, the authors measure wavefunction properties to identify phase boundaries.
result: Five distinct phases are observed: extended, localized, and three types of critical phases, with clear signatures in transport and entanglement measures.
conclusion: The work demonstrates the richness of localization phenomena in driven systems and provides a platform for studying critical phases.

tldr: This paper studies the nonequilibrium expansion dynamics of dipolar bosons and fermions in 1D optical lattices using a numerically exact many-body method.
motivation: Understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics in dipolar quantum gases is important for probing many-body correlations and quantum fragmentation.
method: The authors use the multiconfigurational time-dependent Hartree method to simulate the expansion dynamics of dipolar atoms in a finite one-dimensional lattice.
result: They observe distinct expansion behaviors for bosons and fermions, influenced by dipolar interactions and lattice depth.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the role of correlations and interactions in nonequilibrium dynamics of dipolar systems.

title: Adiabatic Transition Between Floquet And Bloch Topological Modes
authors: Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, And Wenjing Zhang

We investigated the trimer optical lattice subject to Floquet modulation along the propagation direction. Numerical calculations and finite element simulations show that such Floquet modulation can induce localized edge states, whose optical fields exhibit spatial oscillations. Quasienergy band anal…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063513] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological edge states in a trimer optical lattice, focusing on adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch modes.
motivation: To understand how Floquet modulation can create localized edge states and how these states transition adiabatically to Bloch modes.
method: Numerical calculations and finite element simulations of a trimer optical lattice with Floquet modulation along the propagation direction.
result: Floquet modulation induces localized edge states with spatial oscillations; quasienergy band analysis reveals topological properties.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a mechanism for controlling topological modes via adiabatic transitions in driven optical lattices.

title: Polarization-based Indices In Quantum Many-body Systems: Validity And Extension Beyond One Dimension
authors: Yasuhiro Tada
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuhiro Tada

The expectation value of the twist operator has been widely used as a polarization-based index for gapped and gapless phases in interacting quantum many-body systems. Although numerous studies support this usage in specific settings, and rigorous results have established the validity of the criterio…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235118] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polarization-based indices (twist operator expectation values) as topological invariants in quantum many-body systems, extending their validity to one-dimensional gapless phases and two-dimensional systems.
motivation: Polarization-based indices are widely used to characterize topological phases, but their validity beyond one-dimensional gapped systems is not fully established. The author aims to clarify the conditions under which these indices remain reliable.
method: The author analyzes the twist operator expectation value using analytical arguments and numerical simulations for various models, including one-dimensional gapless systems and two-dimensional systems with and without interactions.
result: The polarization index is shown to be valid for one-dimensional gapless phases under certain conditions, but its extension to two dimensions is problematic due to ambiguities in defining the twist operator and sensitivity to boundary conditions.
conclusion: Polarization-based indices are not universally applicable beyond one-dimensional gapped systems; careful consideration of the system's properties is required when using them as topological invariants.

title: Spin Dependence Of Charge Dynamics And Group Velocity In Chiral Molecules

motivation: Understanding the transient dynamics of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) is important for spintronics and molecular electronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: Time-dependent quantum-transport simulations are used to model the transient CISS dynamics in chiral molecules.
result: The paper reports spin-dependent charge dynamics and group velocity in chiral molecules.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of CISS but are not directly relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Spectral Decimation Of Quantum Many-body Hamiltonians

We develop a systematic theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians and show that it provides a quantitative probe of emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra. Building on an analytical description of statistical mixtures, we derive an explicit expression for the size …

tldr: Develops a theory of spectral decimation for quantum many-body Hamiltonians to probe emergent symmetries in mixed spectra.
motivation: To provide a quantitative method for detecting emergent symmetries in statistically mixed spectra of quantum many-body systems.
method: Derives an analytical expression for spectral decimation based on statistical mixtures of spectra.
result: Obtains an explicit expression for the size of spectral decimation and demonstrates its use as a probe of emergent symmetries.
conclusion: Spectral decimation offers a new tool for analyzing quantum many-body Hamiltonians, particularly for mixed spectra.

result: Quasiparticle lifetime agrees with theory at higher temperatures but deviates at lower temperatures.

title: Finite-temperature Topological Transitions In The Presence Of Quenched Uncorrelated Disorder

We address issues related to the presence of defects at finite-temperature topological transitions, in particular when defects are modeled in terms of further variables associated with a quenched disorder, corresponding to the limit in which the defect dynamics is very slow. As a paradigmatic model,…

tldr: This paper studies finite-temperature topological transitions in the presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder, focusing on defect dynamics.
motivation: To understand how quenched disorder affects topological phase transitions at finite temperature, which is relevant for condensed matter systems with slow defect dynamics.
method: The authors use a paradigmatic model and analytical/numerical methods to analyze the effects of quenched disorder on topological transitions.
result: They find that quenched disorder can modify the nature of topological transitions, potentially leading to new phases or altered critical behavior.
conclusion: The presence of quenched uncorrelated disorder significantly impacts finite-temperature topological transitions, and the results provide insights into defect behavior in disordered systems.

title: Mathematical Model Of The Amoeba-inspired Combinatorial Optimization Machine For Physical Implementation And Its Equivalence To Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Yusuke Miyajima And Masahito Mochizuki

motivation: To design a physical combinatorial optimization machine with high efficiency and low power consumption, inspired by slime mold behavior.
method: The authors propose a mathematical model suitable for physical implementation and prove its equivalence to recurrent neural networks.
result: The model is equivalent to recurrent neural networks, enabling analysis of dynamics and performance.
conclusion: The equivalence suggests that the amoeba-inspired machine can be realized using existing neural network hardware, but the work is not directly aligned with the user's research interests.
