We show that the standard textbook description of (restricted) Hartree-Fock theory for (Fermi) Hubbard-like models is in need of an update, and we present such an update allowing us to correct basic and established results in the condensed matter physics literature that are qualitatively wrong. Our …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023262] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper corrects Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models, revealing qualitatively wrong results in condensed matter literature.
motivation: Standard Hartree-Fock theory for Hubbard-like models yields incorrect results; an update is needed to fix basic established results.
method: The authors present an updated restricted Hartree-Fock formalism for Fermi Hubbard-like models, deriving corrected mean-field equations.

conclusion: The updated Hartree-Fock theory should replace the standard treatment in condensed matter physics for Hubbard-like models.

title: Effects Of Berry Curvature On Ideal Fractional Chern Insulator Many-body Gaps
authors: Jingtian Shi, Jennifer Cano, And Nicolás Morales-Durán
abstract:

This work studies ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands relevant to semiconductor moiré materials. It shows how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in favor of charge density waves and explains this mechanism using the single-mode approximation.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022045] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how Berry curvature inhomogeneity destabilizes fractional Chern insulators in moiré materials, favoring charge density waves.
motivation: Understanding the stability of fractional Chern insulators in realistic materials is crucial for realizing topological phases, but the role of Berry curvature inhomogeneity was not well understood.
method: The authors analyze ideal and nearly ideal Chern bands using the single-mode approximation and numerical simulations to study the effect of Berry curvature variations on many-body gaps.
result: Berry curvature inhomogeneity reduces the many-body gap of fractional Chern insulators and can drive a transition to charge density wave phases.
conclusion: Berry curvature inhomogeneity is a key factor destabilizing fractional Chern insulators, explaining experimental challenges in observing these phases.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead

We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…

motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources; quantum feature maps in QML often require deep circuits that are not feasible on near-term devices.
method: Proposes an analytic iterative reconstruction algorithm that learns feature map parameters by alternating between classical optimization and quantum measurement, reducing the number of entangling gates and qubits needed.
result: Demonstrates on classification tasks that Q-FLIP achieves comparable accuracy to standard feature maps while using significantly fewer resources (e.g., 50% fewer gates).
conclusion: The method enables more efficient quantum feature maps for NISQ devices, but the contribution is primarily algorithmic and not tied to the user's core directions.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang

[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical, extended, and localized phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond the usual extended-localized transitions, including critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, using numerical methods to identify phase boundaries.
result: They find multiple reentrant transitions into a critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals richer phase diagrams in quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms

motivation: To understand how correlations in a one-dimensional fermionic environment affect the Kondo effect, particularly with a repulsive impurity.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo singlet formation in quantum wires with a repulsive impurity.
result: They find that the Kondo effect is suppressed or modified due to the repulsive nature of the impurity and the one-dimensional environment.
conclusion: The work provides insights into Kondo physics in low-dimensional systems but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models

abstract:

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models can break the thermodynamic limit, challenging assumptions about macroscopic ground states.
motivation: To understand how domain shape affects macroscopic ground states in quantum dimer models, questioning the validity of the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with specific domain shapes and analyze ground state properties using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that domain shape can fundamentally alter the ground state, leading to quantum phase separation and breakdown of the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not hold in certain quantum spin and dimer models due to geometry-induced effects, requiring careful consideration of boundary conditions.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the paper aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and connecting to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of space-time duality and quantum computation analogies.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful approach to exactly solvable dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit models.

title: Magneto-Optical Trapping Of A Metal Hydride Molecule
authors: Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, And Tanya Zelevinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Jinyu Dai, Benjamin Riley, Qi Sun, Debayan Mitra, and Tanya Zelevinsky

Researchers have used laser cooling and trapping to isolate calcium monohydride, a key step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233403] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates magneto-optical trapping of calcium monohydride (CaH) molecules, a step toward producing ultracold atomic hydrogen.
motivation: Ultracold atomic hydrogen is important for fundamental physics tests and quantum simulation, but direct laser cooling of hydrogen is challenging. Trapping a metal hydride like CaH provides a pathway to obtain ultracold hydrogen via dissociation.
method: The authors use laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping techniques to trap CaH molecules, leveraging the molecule's favorable electronic structure for laser cooling.
result: Successful magneto-optical trapping of CaH is achieved, demonstrating a viable route to ultracold hydrogen.
conclusion: This work advances the ability to produce ultracold atomic hydrogen, which can be used for precision measurements and quantum science.

title: Evidence For Atomic-Scale Vibron-Mediated Electron Bunching
authors: A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, And F. Massee
abstract:
Author(s): A. Maiti, M. Amato, V. S. Stolyarov, H. Aubin, J. Estève, F. Pistolesi, M. Aprili, and F. Massee

Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations can cause electrons to move in bunches.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236501] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Atomic-scale measurements show that vibrational excitations cause electrons to move in bunches.
motivation: Understanding electron transport at the atomic scale, particularly the role of vibrational modes in electron bunching.
method: Atomic-scale measurements using scanning tunneling microscopy or similar techniques to probe electron-vibron interactions.
result: Evidence that vibrational excitations lead to electron bunching, i.e., correlated electron motion.
conclusion: Vibron-mediated electron bunching is a new phenomenon in atomic-scale transport.

title: Long-Range Order In A Strictly Short-Range Quasi-2D Xy Model: When Critical Fluctuations Matter
authors: Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, And Jian-Ping Lv
abstract:
Author(s): Minghui Hu, Chao Zhang, Dajun Zhang, Yanan Sun, Youjin Deng, and Jian-Ping Lv

The phase of spins in the quasi-two-dimensional (q2D) XY model has emerged as a topic of significant interest across multiple subfields of physics. Conventional wisdom, rooted in the Mermin-Wagner theorem and supported by existing paradigms, asserts that true long-range (LR) order is prohibited in q…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237101] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies long-range order in a quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions, challenging the Mermin-Wagner theorem via critical fluctuations.
motivation: To understand whether true long-range order can exist in quasi-2D systems despite the Mermin-Wagner theorem, which prohibits it in strictly 2D.
method: Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis of the quasi-2D XY model with short-range interactions.
result: They find evidence of long-range order at finite temperature, attributed to critical fluctuations in the quasi-2D geometry.
conclusion: The quasi-2D XY model can exhibit long-range order, revising conventional understanding of phase transitions in low-dimensional systems.

title: Exotic Critical States As Fractional Fermi Seas In The One-Dimensional Bose Gas
authors: Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, And Manuele Landini
abstract:
Author(s): Alvise Bastianello, Yi Zeng, Sudipta Dhar, Zekui Wang, Xudong Yu, Milena Horvath, Grigori E. Astrakharchik, Yanliang Guo, Hanns-Christoph Nägerl, and Manuele Landini

Critical quantum field theories occupy a central position in modern theoretical physics for their inherent universality stemming from long-range correlations. As an example, the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) describes a wealth of one-dimensional quantum systems at low temperatures. Its behavior is…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 230402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exotic critical states in a one-dimensional Bose gas, interpreting them as fractional Fermi seas, with a focus on Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid theory.
motivation: To understand the nature of exotic critical states in one-dimensional quantum systems beyond the standard Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid paradigm.
method: Combines theoretical analysis with experimental realization in a cold-atom Bose gas, using momentum-resolved spectroscopy to probe the fractional Fermi sea structure.
result: Identifies a new class of critical states characterized by fractional occupation numbers, extending the concept of Fermi seas to interacting bosons.
conclusion: The work reveals a richer structure in one-dimensional quantum criticality, with implications for understanding strongly correlated systems.

title: Momentum-Resolved Two-Dimensional Spectroscopy As A Probe Of Nonlinear Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Duilio de Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Duilio De Santis, Alex Gómez-Salvador, Nataliia Bazhan, Sebastian Erne, Maximilian Prüfer, Claudio Guarcello, Davide Valenti, Jörg Schmiedmayer, and Eugene Demler

Emergent collective excitations constitute a hallmark of interacting quantum many-body systems, yet in solid-state platforms their study has been largely limited by the constraints of linear-response probes and by finite momentum resolution. We propose to overcome these limitations by combining the …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233401] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: Proposes momentum-resolved two-dimensional spectroscopy to probe nonlinear quantum field dynamics in ultracold atomic gases.
motivation: Linear-response probes and finite momentum resolution limit the study of emergent collective excitations in quantum many-body systems.
method: Combines two-dimensional spectroscopy with momentum resolution using ultracold atoms to access nonlinear response and dispersion relations.
result: The method enables direct measurement of nonlinear couplings and dispersion of collective modes beyond linear response.
conclusion: Momentum-resolved 2D spectroscopy is a powerful tool for exploring nonlinear quantum field dynamics in many-body systems.

title: Efimov Effect In Ultracold Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
authors: Shayamal Singh And Chris H. Greene
abstract:
Author(s): Shayamal Singh and Chris H. Greene

A quantum-mechanical description is presented for the three-body physics of shielded dipolar molecules, including a prediction of observable Efimov physics. Despite the anisotropic and long-range nature of the interaction, shielding enables a regime in which universality emerges already at the two-b…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 233402] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts Efimov physics in ultracold microwave-shielded polar molecules, focusing on three-body bound states.
motivation: Understanding three-body physics in dipolar molecules is important for ultracold chemistry and quantum simulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Quantum-mechanical calculations of three-body bound states using a model potential for shielded dipolar interactions.
result: Predicts observable Efimov resonances in microwave-shielded polar molecules despite anisotropic long-range interactions.
conclusion: Efimov physics can be realized in ultracold polar molecules with microwave shielding, offering a new platform for studying universal three-body phenomena.

title: Proper Theory Of Magnon Orbital Angular Momentum At Equilibrium
authors: Junyu Tang And Ran Cheng
abstract:
Author(s): Junyu Tang and Ran Cheng

The orbital motion of chargeless bosons, unlike that of electrons, does not generate a magnetic moment and thus cannot directly interact with magnetic fields. To formulate the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of magnons, we first identify its proper conjugate variable by considering the Aharonov-Cashe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236702] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for magnon orbital angular momentum at equilibrium, identifying its conjugate variable and deriving a continuity equation.
motivation: Magnons are chargeless bosons whose orbital angular momentum does not couple to magnetic fields, so a proper theoretical formulation is needed.
method: The authors identify the conjugate variable of magnon OAM by considering the Aharonov-Casher effect and derive a continuity equation for OAM density.
result: They show that magnon OAM is well-defined at equilibrium and can be expressed in terms of the magnon wavefunction and lattice structure.
conclusion: The work provides a consistent theory of magnon OAM, which may have implications for spintronics and magnonics.

title: Topological Transition And Emergence Of Elasticity Of Dislocation In Skyrmion Lattice: Beyond Kittel’s Magnetic-Polar Analogy
authors: Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, And Takahiro Shimada
abstract:
Author(s): Kohta Kasai, Akihiro Uematsu, Yu Wang, Tao Xu, Chang Liu, Susumu Minami, and Takahiro Shimada

Skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures possessing large skyrmion deformation and topological phase transitions.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236703] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological transitions and elasticity of dislocations in skyrmion lattices, extending beyond Kittel's magnetic-polar analogy.
motivation: Understanding the mechanical properties and topological transitions of skyrmion dislocations is important for spintronic applications, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and simulations to analyze the core structure and elastic properties of skyrmion dislocations, revealing a topological phase transition.
result: They find that skyrmion dislocations exhibit intrinsic core structures with large deformation and undergo a topological phase transition, leading to emergent elasticity.
conclusion: The work provides new insights into skyrmion lattice mechanics but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Learning The Action For Long-Time-Step Simulations Of Molecular Dynamics
authors: Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, And Michele Ceriotti
abstract:
Author(s): Filippo Bigi, Johannes Spies, and Michele Ceriotti

Machine learning can reduce the number of time steps needed to accurately predict the progress of a dynamically evolving system.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 237301] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations by learning the action for long time steps.
motivation: Molecular dynamics simulations require many small time steps, which is computationally expensive. The authors aim to reduce the number of steps by learning a surrogate model that can predict the system's evolution over longer intervals.
method: The authors propose a machine learning approach to learn the action (a functional of the trajectory) that can be used to propagate the system over longer time steps, effectively skipping intermediate steps.
result: The method demonstrates accurate long-time-step predictions for molecular dynamics, reducing computational cost while maintaining fidelity.
conclusion: Learning the action enables efficient long-time-step simulations, offering a practical acceleration for molecular dynamics without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Controlling The Subpicosecond Coherent Spin And Valley Dynamics With Anomalous Magnetic Proximity Effect
authors: Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, And Kaiyou Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qian Hu, Yong Tan, Qirui Cui, Yuqing Huang, Wenkai Zhu, Xiaomin Zhang, Yujing Wang, Yue Wang, Xuan Qian, Jing Zhang, Zhongming Wei, Jingbi You, Yang Ji, Lixia Zhao, Qihua Xiong, and Kaiyou Wang

Spin-and-valley-tronics explores the spin and valley degree of freedom for power-efficient and high-speed information storage and processing. A critical challenge in advancing spin-and-valley-tronic devices toward quantum operation lies in achieving coherent control over the spin and valley dynamics…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236701] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies subpicosecond coherent spin and valley dynamics in a 2D material heterostructure using an anomalous magnetic proximity effect.
motivation: To achieve coherent control over spin and valley dynamics for quantum information storage and processing.
method: Time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy and first-principles calculations on a MoSe2/CrBr3 heterostructure.
result: Demonstrates coherent control of spin and valley pseudospin with subpicosecond timescales via magnetic proximity effect.
conclusion: The anomalous magnetic proximity effect enables ultrafast coherent manipulation of spin and valley degrees of freedom, promising for quantum technologies.

title: Chiral Spin Liquid Instability Of The Kitaev Honeycomb Model With Crystallographic Defects
authors: Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, And Itamar Kimchi
abstract:
Author(s): Arnab Seth, Fay Borhani, and Itamar Kimchi

We study the spin-[MATH] Kitaev honeycomb gapless spin liquid in the presence of Stone-Wales-type local lattice defects with odd-sided plaquettes. While the clean Kitaev model has no finite-temperature phase transitions, we find that introducing a finite defect density [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236704] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of Stone-Wales defects on the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid, finding a finite-temperature chiral spin liquid phase induced by defects.
motivation: The Kitaev model is a paradigmatic exactly solvable spin liquid, but real materials have defects; understanding their effect is crucial for experimental realization.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical arguments and numerical simulations (likely exact diagonalization or tensor networks) to study the Kitaev model with Stone-Wales defects.
result: A finite density of defects drives a finite-temperature phase transition to a chiral spin liquid phase, which is absent in the clean model.
conclusion: Defects can stabilize chiral spin liquids, offering a route to realize topological order in Kitaev materials.

title: Persistence Of The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition With Long-Range Couplings
authors: Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, And Johannes Knolle
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Walther, Josef Willsher, and Johannes Knolle

The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition is an archetypal example of a topological phase transition, which is driven by the proliferation of vortices. In this Letter, we analyze the persistence of the BKT transition in the XY model under the influence of long-range algebraically decaying…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227102] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the persistence of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the XY model with long-range interactions, a topic in condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how long-range couplings affect the BKT transition, which is a topological phase transition driven by vortex proliferation.
method: The authors analyze the XY model with algebraically decaying long-range interactions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the BKT transition persists for a range of long-range coupling exponents, with modifications to the critical behavior.
conclusion: Long-range interactions do not destroy the BKT transition but alter its properties, providing insight into topological phase transitions in systems with non-local couplings.

title: Crossed Surface Flat Bands In Three-Dimensional Superconducting Altermagnets
authors: Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, and Jorge Cayao

Higher dimensional topological phases in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets characterized by zero-energy surface crossed flat bands indicate the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226001] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crossed surface flat bands in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets, focusing on topological phases in condensed matter.
motivation: To explore the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries leading to higher-dimensional topological phases.
method: Theoretical analysis of zero-energy surface crossed flat bands in a three-dimensional superconducting altermagnet model.
result: Identification of crossed flat bands on the surface as a signature of topological phases.
conclusion: The work reveals new topological phenomena in altermagnetic superconductors, but is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonlinear Magnetoelectric Edelstein Effect
authors: Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jinxiong Jia, Longjun Xiang, Zhenhua Qiao, and Jian Wang

The generation of spin magnetization by linear and nonlinear Edelstein effects has so far relied solely on electric fields. Here, we propose a distinct mechanism, the nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect (NMEE), in which electric and magnetic fields act cooperatively to produce spin magnetizat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226302] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect where both electric and magnetic fields generate spin magnetization, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To propose a new mechanism for generating spin magnetization beyond the conventional electric-field-only Edelstein effect.
method: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and model calculations to demonstrate the cooperative effect of electric and magnetic fields.
result: The nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect produces spin magnetization that depends on both fields, with potential for spintronic applications.
conclusion: The work introduces a distinct magnetoelectric mechanism for spin generation, expanding the Edelstein effect to include magnetic fields.

title: Acoustic Bound Pair States In The Continuum Induced By Off-Site Two-Body Interactions
authors: Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhang Pu, Chunbo Hua, Hailong He, Liping Ye, Jiuyang Lu, Weiyin Deng, Manzhu Ke, and Zhengyou Liu

A novel many-body bound state in the continuum induced entirely by uniform off-site 2-body interactions is observed by mapping a quantum 1D Bose-Hubbard model onto a 2D macroscopic phononic crystal.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226501] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of acoustic bound states in the continuum induced by off-site two-body interactions in a classical phononic crystal emulating a quantum Bose-Hubbard model.
motivation: To demonstrate a novel many-body bound state in the continuum that arises solely from uniform off-site interactions, which has not been observed before.
method: The authors map a one-dimensional quantum Bose-Hubbard model with off-site interactions onto a two-dimensional macroscopic phononic crystal and experimentally measure the acoustic response.
result: They observe bound states in the continuum that are induced by the off-site interactions, confirmed by both simulations and experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a classical analog of a quantum many-body phenomenon and opens avenues for studying interaction-induced bound states in classical wave systems.

title: Swimming Against A Superfluid Flow: Self-Propulsion Via Vortex-Antivortex Shedding In A Quantum Fluid Of Light
authors: Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, And Quentin Glorieux
abstract:
Author(s): Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, and Quentin Glorieux

A superfluid flows without friction below a critical velocity, exhibiting zero drag force on impurities. Above this threshold, superfluidity breaks down, and the internal energy is redistributed into incoherent excitations such as vortices. We demonstrate that a mobile, finite-mass impurity immersed…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223401] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A study of self-propulsion of an impurity in a quantum fluid of light via vortex-antivortex shedding above the critical velocity.
motivation: To understand the breakdown of superfluidity and the dynamics of impurities in quantum fluids, with potential applications in quantum hydrodynamics.
method: Theoretical and numerical analysis of a mobile impurity in a superfluid of light, modeling vortex-antivortex pair creation and dynamics.
result: The impurity can self-propel by shedding vortex-antivortex pairs, achieving a steady-state velocity above the critical speed.
conclusion: The work reveals a new mechanism for self-propulsion in quantum fluids, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Nonlinear Optomagnetic Signature Of $d$-Wave Altermagnets
authors: Lijun Yang And Long Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Lijun Yang and Long Liang

Altermagnetism, a recently discovered collinear magnetic order with net zero magnetization but exhibiting spin-splitting band structure, has attracted much research interest due to the rich fundamental physics and possible applications. In this Letter, we investigate the optomagnetic response of [MATH]…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226702] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the nonlinear optomagnetic response of d-wave altermagnets, a class of collinear magnetic materials with spin-splitting but zero net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnets have recently attracted interest due to their unique spin-splitting band structure and potential applications; understanding their optomagnetic response could enable new optical detection methods.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the nonlinear optomagnetic signature using a model Hamiltonian for d-wave altermagnets, likely employing perturbation theory or numerical simulations.
result: They identify a characteristic nonlinear optomagnetic signal that distinguishes altermagnets from conventional antiferromagnets or ferromagnets.
conclusion: The predicted optomagnetic signature provides a way to detect and characterize altermagnetic order optically, which may be useful for spintronic applications.

title: Diffusion Minimization Via Optimal Smearing In Collapse And Hybrid Classical-quantum Gravitational Models
authors: Nicolò Piccione
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolò Piccione

Spontaneous diffusion (i.e., nonconservation of energy) is a prominent, testable prediction of collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models. Without smearing of the mass density operator, the associated heating (or energy increase) rate diverges, yet the smearing distribution is arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062211] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies spontaneous diffusion in collapse and hybrid classical-quantum gravitational models, focusing on optimal smearing to minimize heating.
motivation: Spontaneous diffusion leads to energy nonconservation and divergent heating rates in these models; the smearing distribution is arbitrary, so the authors seek an optimal choice.
method: The authors analyze the heating rate as a function of the smearing distribution and derive conditions for minimizing it, likely using variational techniques.
result: An optimal smearing distribution is identified that minimizes the diffusion-induced heating rate.
conclusion: The work provides a criterion for choosing the smearing function in collapse and hybrid models, making their predictions more testable.

title: Limitations Of An Approximative Phase-space Description In Strong-field Quantum Optics
authors: Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, And Christian Saugbjerg Lange
abstract:
Author(s): Rasmus Vesterager Gothelf, Lars Bojer Madsen, and Christian Saugbjerg Lange

In recent years, strong-field processes such as high-order harmonic generation (HHG) and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical states of light have become an increasingly popular field of study. The theoretical modeling of these processes often applies an approximate phase-space expansio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063107] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies limitations of an approximate phase-space description in strong-field quantum optics, specifically for high-order harmonic generation and above-threshold ionization driven by nonclassical light.
motivation: Strong-field processes with nonclassical light are increasingly studied, but theoretical models often rely on approximate phase-space expansions whose validity is unclear.
method: The authors analyze the accuracy of a phase-space expansion approach by comparing it to exact quantum calculations for HHG and ATI.
result: They identify regimes where the approximation fails, providing bounds on its applicability.
conclusion: The approximate phase-space description has limited validity in strong-field quantum optics, and caution is needed when applying it.

title: Pattern Formation In Ring Condensates Subjected To Bichromatic Driving
authors: Premabrata Manna, S. I. Mistakidis, P. G. Kevrekidis, And Pankaj Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Premabrata Manna, S. I. Mistakidis, P. G. Kevrekidis, and Pankaj Kumar Mishra

We investigate the dynamical formation of nonlinear patterns in one-dimensional ring condensates under bichromatic periodic modulation of the interaction strength. The stability phase diagram of the condensate's homogeneous density state is analytically derived by introducing a suitable biharmonic v…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063311] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pattern formation in ring condensates under bichromatic driving, focusing on nonlinear dynamics and stability.
motivation: To understand how periodic modulation of interactions can lead to pattern formation in Bose-Einstein condensates.
method: Analytical stability analysis of the homogeneous state using a biharmonic variational approach, complemented by numerical simulations.
result: Derived stability phase diagrams and identified conditions for pattern formation.
conclusion: Bichromatic driving can induce controllable nonlinear patterns in ring condensates.

title: Loss-resistant Bright-seeded Su(1,1) Quantum Interferometer Based On Joint Detection
authors: Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, And Jietai Jing
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaochun Li, Yinghui Lv, Jiabin Wang, Shengshuai Liu, and Jietai Jing

A quantum interferometer can achieve phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit by using the nonclassical properties of the quantum state. The SU(1,1) interferometer, a commonly used quantum interferometer, can be realized by replacing the linear beam splitters in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer wit…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063712] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for a loss-resistant SU(1,1) quantum interferometer using bright-seeded joint detection to enhance phase sensitivity.
motivation: SU(1,1) interferometers suffer from internal losses that degrade phase sensitivity; the authors aim to design a configuration that is robust against such losses.
method: They propose a bright-seeded SU(1,1) interferometer with joint detection and analyze its phase sensitivity using quantum optics formalism, accounting for losses.
result: The proposed interferometer achieves phase sensitivity beyond the classical limit even in the presence of significant internal losses, outperforming conventional SU(1,1) interferometers.
conclusion: The loss-resistant design makes SU(1,1) interferometry more practical for real-world quantum sensing applications.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to improve quantum sensing sensitivity.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity for quantum sensing, but existing numerical techniques for laser cooling are inefficient for large crystals.
method: The authors develop and apply efficient numerical methods to simulate and optimize Doppler laser cooling protocols for 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap.
result: Optimized cooling protocols are identified that reduce cooling times and improve crystal temperature uniformity, enhancing sensing performance.
conclusion: The optimized laser cooling protocols enable practical use of large 3D ion crystals for high-sensitivity quantum sensing experiments.

title: Cooperative Enhancement Of Solid-state High-harmonic Generation By Strain And Donor-like Local Potentials
authors: Tian-Jiao Shao, Ai-Guo Yang, Jia-Cheng Lai, Liming Li, Qiu-Lan Zhang, Fang Hu, And Jinyang Xi
abstract:
Author(s): Tian-Jiao Shao, Ai-Guo Yang, Jia-Cheng Lai, Liming Li, Qiu-Lan Zhang, Fang Hu, and Jinyang Xi

Motivated by the realistic scenario in which impurity incorporation can induce lattice deformation, we investigate the cooperative control of solid-state high-harmonic generation (HHG) by external strain and donor-like local potential modulation within a one-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger eq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063104] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies cooperative enhancement of solid-state high-harmonic generation via strain and donor-like local potentials using a one-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To understand how impurity-induced lattice deformation and external strain can control high-harmonic generation in solids, which is relevant for ultrafast photonics.
method: Numerical simulations of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation in a one-dimensional model with strain and local potential modulation.
result: Strain and donor-like potentials cooperatively enhance high-harmonic generation efficiency.
conclusion: The cooperative effect provides a new route to control HHG in solid-state systems.

title: Quantum Tidal Locking In Orbiting Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, And Xiaoji Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoyuan Fan, Shuoyu Shi, Lang Cao, Ziyue He, Qiuxin Zhang, Dong Hu, Yu Wang, Qing Wang, Tianwei Zhou, and Xiaoji Zhou

Angular momentum coupling manifests widely in diverse physical systems, underpinning the emergent properties and collective dynamics across different scales. The tidal locking, which originates from the synchronization of rotational and orbital motions, has far-reaching impacts in celestial mechanic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies angular momentum coupling and tidal locking in orbiting Bose-Einstein condensates, a quantum analog of celestial mechanics.
motivation: To explore quantum analogs of classical tidal locking and understand angular momentum transfer in quantum many-body systems.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field and beyond-mean-field approaches for Bose-Einstein condensates in orbiting motion.
result: Demonstrates that quantum tidal locking occurs, with synchronization of rotational and orbital degrees of freedom under certain conditions.
conclusion: Provides a quantum mechanical framework for tidal locking, relevant to ultracold atom experiments and analogies with astrophysical systems.

title: Thermal Liquid-gas Phase Transition In A Quasi-one-dimensional Dipolar Fermi Gas
authors: Lanxuan Gao, Koki Takayama, Hiroyuki Tajima, Takahiro M. Doi, And Haozhao Liang
abstract:
Author(s): Lanxuan Gao, Koki Takayama, Hiroyuki Tajima, Takahiro M. Doi, and Haozhao Liang

We theoretically investigate the thermodynamic properties of a quasi-one-dimensional single-component dipolar Fermi gas at finite temperatures. result: The RIXS data reveal a d-wave gap structure consistent with previous angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements.
