title: Evolution Of Crystal Field And Intra-ionic Interactions In Ilmenite $A{\mathrm{IrO}}_{3}$ ($A=\mathrm{Mg}$, Zn, Cd) And Hyperhoneycomb $β\text{−}{\mathrm{ZnIrO}}_{3}$
authors: Yuya Haraguchi, Hiroko Aruga Katori, Kenji Ishii, And Hakuto Suzuki
abstract:
Author(s): Yuya Haraguchi, Hiroko Aruga Katori, Kenji Ishii, and Hakuto Suzuki

Spin-orbit Mott insulators with the [MATH] electron configuration are promising platforms for the Kitaev spin liquid, yet fine-tuning of their crystal structures is essential to suppress non-Kitaev interactions. Here, we investigate the local electronic structures of the ilmenite iridates $A…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235114] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies crystal field and intra-ionic interactions in iridate materials, focusing on spin-orbit Mott insulators and Kitaev spin liquid candidates.
motivation: To understand how crystal structure tuning affects non-Kitaev interactions in iridates, which are promising for realizing Kitaev spin liquids.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and theoretical calculations to probe local electronic structures of ilmenite and hyperhoneycomb iridates.
result: Reveals evolution of crystal field splitting and spin-orbit coupling across different A-site cations and structures.
conclusion: Fine-tuning of crystal structure is essential to suppress non-Kitaev interactions, but the paper does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Supratransmission In Lattices With Purely Nonlinear Coupling
authors: Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Defri Ahmad, Tae-Yeon Kim, Andreas Schiffer, Jinkyu Yang, and Hadi Susanto

Supratransmission is examined in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, extending the phenomenon to systems that lack a linear passband. In contrast to standard lattices with mixed linear-nonlinear interactions, the present model has no linear spectrum, so energy propagation arises entir…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064205] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies supratransmission in nonlinear lattices with purely nonlinear coupling, where energy propagation occurs without a linear passband.
motivation: To extend the phenomenon of supratransmission to systems lacking linear spectrum, which is relevant for understanding energy transport in nonlinear media.
method: The authors analyze a lattice model with purely nonlinear coupling using analytical and numerical methods to characterize supratransmission thresholds and dynamics.
result: They find that supratransmission can occur even without linear modes, with energy propagation driven solely by nonlinear interactions.
conclusion: The work broadens the scope of supratransmission to purely nonlinear systems, offering insights into nonlinear wave propagation.

title: Emergent Metastable Behavior In A Resource-constrained Network Of Exclusion Processes
authors: Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, And Arvind Kumar Gupta
abstract:
Author(s): Nikhil Bhatia, Ashish Kumar Pandey, and Arvind Kumar Gupta

Inspired by the intrinsic organization observed in various biological and physical processes, which manifests through interacting subsystems connected by networks, where particles often compete for limited resources, we study a four-lane network system with a branching-merging geometry under resourc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064122] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies metastable behavior in a resource-constrained network of exclusion processes, a model of interacting particles on a multi-lane network.
motivation: To understand emergent organization in biological and physical systems where particles compete for limited resources in a network geometry.
method: The authors analyze a four-lane network with branching-merging geometry using a resource-constrained exclusion process, likely via mean-field theory or Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They observe emergent metastable states characterized by long-lived particle configurations before eventual relaxation.
conclusion: Resource constraints and network topology can lead to metastable behavior, providing insights into self-organization in complex systems.

title: Pearl Supratransmission In A Boundary-driven Two-dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation With A Hole
authors: Rudy Kusdiantara And Hadi Susanto
abstract:
Author(s): Rudy Kusdiantara and Hadi Susanto

We investigate energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole. Harmonic forcing with azimuthal modulation generates standing-wave states whose existence and stability depend on the driving amplitude, the inner radius, and the imposed …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064204] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies energy supratransmission in a boundary-driven 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a hole, focusing on standing-wave states and their stability.
motivation: To understand nonlinear wave transmission in the presence of a defect (hole) in two dimensions.
method: Numerical simulation and stability analysis of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a central hole and azimuthal modulation.
result: Existence and stability of standing-wave states depend on driving amplitude, inner radius, and azimuthal modulation.
conclusion: The hole can suppress or enhance supratransmission depending on parameters, offering control over energy transfer.

title: Community Detection By The Normalized Ricci Flow With The Optimization Of The Information Entropy
authors: Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, And Jiao Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenli Wang, Silu Wang, Chaoqun Ma, Yi Xiong, Guoqing Chen, and Jiao Gu

Discrete Ricci curvature serves as a fundamental geometric tool for quantifying the structural characteristics of complex networks, effectively capturing the richness of their connection patterns. Building on this theoretical framework, this paper proposes an improved discrete Ricci curvature algori…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064304] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies discrete Ricci flow and information entropy to community detection in complex networks.
motivation: Community detection is important for understanding network structure, and discrete Ricci curvature provides a geometric tool to capture connection patterns.
method: The authors propose an improved discrete Ricci curvature algorithm and combine it with normalized Ricci flow and optimization of information entropy to detect communities.
result: The method effectively identifies community structures in complex networks, as demonstrated on benchmark networks.
conclusion: The proposed approach offers a novel geometric perspective for community detection, leveraging curvature and entropy.

title: Dissipative Response Of Driven Bead-spring-dashpot Chains
authors: R. Kailasham
abstract:
Author(s): R. Kailasham

The work dissipated in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction is numerically calculated by considering a sequence of [MATH] spring-dashpots tethered at one end and being pulled at the other using a harmonic trap via linear and symmetric protocols. The variation of the dissipation with the chain…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065408] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies the dissipated work in pulling a polymer chain with internal friction using a bead-spring-dashpot model.
motivation: Understanding dissipation in driven polymer chains is important for polymer physics and biophysics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors simulate a sequence of spring-dashpots tethered at one end and pulled by a harmonic trap using linear and symmetric protocols, computing the work dissipated.
result: The variation of dissipation with chain length and pulling protocol is characterized numerically.
conclusion: The study provides insights into dissipative response of polymer chains but remains within classical soft matter physics.

title: Controlling The Glass Transition Through Active Fluctuating Interactions
authors: Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, And Thibault Bertrand
abstract:
Author(s): Emir Sezik, Henry Alston, and Thibault Bertrand

Fluctuating pairwise interactions are understood to drive fluidlike states in dense biological systems. These states find a broad range of functionalities, such as directing growth during morphogenesis and forming aggregates with heightened mechanical response. However, a tractable model capturing t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062102] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how active fluctuating interactions control the glass transition in dense biological systems.
motivation: Understanding how fluidlike states arise in dense biological systems is important for morphogenesis and mechanical response.
method: The authors develop a tractable model of fluctuating pairwise interactions and analyze its effect on the glass transition.
result: They find that active fluctuations can drive the system into a fluidlike state, controlling the glass transition.
conclusion: Active fluctuating interactions provide a mechanism to tune the glass transition in biological systems.

title: Linearization Principle: The Geometric Origin Of Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equations
authors: Hiroki Suyari
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroki Suyari

Anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions are observed in various complex systems. To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for these phenomena, we present a geometric derivation of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation by introducing the linearization principle directly at the dynamical st…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064118] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations from a geometric linearization principle, focusing on anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions.
motivation: To provide a consistent dynamical foundation for anomalous diffusion and power-law distributions observed in complex systems.
method: Introduces a linearization principle at the dynamical level to geometrically derive nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations.
result: Presents a geometric derivation of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, linking them to the linearization principle.
conclusion: The linearization principle offers a geometric origin for nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations, potentially explaining anomalous diffusion.

title: Reinforcement Learning For Chemotherapy Scheduling In A Stochastic Tumor Evolution Model
authors: M. Giles And P. K. Newton
abstract:
Author(s): M. Giles and P. K. Newton

We present a [MATH]-learning framework for optimizing chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic finite-cell model of tumor evolution under drug-induced selection. The tumor consists of three competing subpopulations: a chemosensitive lineage, [MATH], and two single-drug-resistant lineages, [MATH] a…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064404] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Uses reinforcement learning to optimize chemotherapy dosing schedules in a stochastic tumor evolution model.
motivation: To improve cancer treatment by finding optimal drug schedules that minimize tumor burden while accounting for drug resistance.
method: Applies Q-learning, a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm, to a stochastic finite-cell model of tumor evolution with three competing subpopulations.
result: The RL agent learns dosing schedules that outperform standard protocols in simulations.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning can effectively optimize chemotherapy scheduling in a stochastic environment, potentially leading to better patient outcomes.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics arguments to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds a universal upper bound for critical temperature determined solely by the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Minority Takeover In Majority Dynamics: Searching For Rare Initializations Via The History Passing Algorithm
authors: Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, And Lenka Zdeborová
abstract:
Author(s): Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, and Lenka Zdeborová

We investigate how much bias in the initial configuration is required to drive global agreement in synchronous, deterministic majority dynamics on large random [MATH]-regular graphs. Nodes take values [MATH] and update their states at each discrete time step to align with the majority of their neighbors.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how initial bias influences global agreement in majority dynamics on random regular graphs, using a history passing algorithm to find rare initializations.
motivation: Understanding the minimal bias needed for a minority to take over in majority dynamics is relevant to consensus problems in distributed computing and social networks.
method: The authors analyze synchronous deterministic majority dynamics on large random regular graphs and develop a history passing algorithm to search for rare initial configurations that lead to minority takeover.
result: They find that a small bias in the initial configuration can drive global agreement, and the history passing algorithm efficiently identifies such initializations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the sensitivity of majority dynamics to initial conditions and offers a computational tool for exploring rare events in such systems.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks, a physical neural network model.
motivation: To understand how physical constraints affect learning dynamics and memory retention in neuromorphic systems.
method: The authors train differentiable resistor networks sequentially on multiple tasks and analyze forgetting using Kirchhoff's laws.
result: They observe catastrophic forgetting similar to artificial neural networks, with some mitigation due to physical constraints.
conclusion: Physical neural networks face similar challenges in continual learning, suggesting the need for specialized algorithms.

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, and J. A. Plascak

The ferromagnetic spin-2 quantum Blume-Capel model in the presence of a transverse crystal field interaction is studied by employing a variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for the free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state. The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamic properties of a quantum spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using variational methods.
motivation: To understand the phase diagram and critical behavior of a higher-spin quantum spin model with transverse crystal field, which is a generalization of the Blume-Capel model.
method: A variational approach based on the Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state.
result: Thermodynamic properties and phase boundaries are obtained, showing the influence of the transverse crystal field on the phase transitions.
conclusion: The model exhibits rich phase diagrams with first- and second-order transitions, but the work is purely in condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. At first, the transfer matrices are analyzed in three representations, i.e., Clifford algebraic representation, transfer …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical solution of the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
motivation: Extend the exactly solvable 2D Ising model to include next-nearest neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Uses transfer matrices in Clifford algebraic, transfer matrix, and other representations to derive the partition function and spontaneous magnetization.
result: Obtains analytic expressions for the partition function and spontaneous magnetization for the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions at zero field.
conclusion: Provides an exact solution for a more complex Ising model, contributing to the theory of phase transitions and critical phenomena.

title: Biologically Relevant Finite-size Effects In A Driven Lattice Gas With Particle Pausing And Dynamical Defects
authors: Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, And Luca Ciandrini
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, and Luca Ciandrini

In this article we present a comprehensive study of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), a model initially introduced to describe RNAP dynamics during transcription. We extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate that the pTASEP is equivalent to …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064114] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven lattice gas model with particle pausing and dynamical defects, motivated by biological transcription, and extends mean-field approaches.
motivation: The model aims to describe RNA polymerase dynamics during transcription, capturing finite-size effects and defects.
method: The authors extend previous mean-field approaches and analyze the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP).
result: They demonstrate equivalence of pTASEP to other models and characterize finite-size effects.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive study of a biologically motivated transport model, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction: Classical Diagonalization Of Hamiltonians In Subspaces Selected By Quantum Computers
authors: Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, And Yuya O. Nakagawa
abstract:
Author(s): Keita Kanno, Masaya Kohda, Ryosuke Imai, Sho Koh, Kosuke Mitarai, Wataru Mizukami, and Yuya O. Nakagawa

We propose quantum-selected configuration interaction, a class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms for calculating the ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians on noisy quantum devices. Suppose that an approximate ground state can be prepared on a quantum computer either b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023268] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for computing ground- and excited-state energies of many-electron Hamiltonians using quantum computers to select important configurations for classical diagonalization.
motivation: To leverage noisy quantum devices for quantum chemistry calculations by combining quantum state preparation with classical diagonalization to reduce quantum resource requirements.
method: The algorithm prepares an approximate ground state on a quantum computer, measures in the computational basis to identify important Slater determinants, and then performs classical configuration interaction in the selected subspace.
result: The method achieves accurate energies for small molecules with fewer quantum resources than full quantum phase estimation, demonstrating robustness to noise.
conclusion: Quantum-selected configuration interaction is a promising approach for near-term quantum chemistry on noisy quantum devices, balancing accuracy and resource requirements.

title: Trapping And Cooling Mechanisms In Blue-detuned Magneto-optical Traps Of Molecules
authors: Qinshu Lyu And M. R. Tarbutt
abstract:
Author(s): Qinshu Lyu and M. R. Tarbutt

This work identifies the mechanisms responsible for trapping and cooling in a blue-detuned magneto-optical trap driven by a pair of closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization. When the Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference between the two components, there is a state that is dark to the beam propagating in one direction but not to the beam from the opposite direction, generating a radiation pressure force toward the field zero.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023259] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies trapping and cooling mechanisms in blue-detuned magneto-optical traps for molecules, focusing on radiation pressure forces from dark states.
motivation: Understanding the mechanisms behind blue-detuned magneto-optical traps (MOTs) for molecules is important for advancing molecular cooling and trapping techniques.
method: The authors analyze a blue-detuned MOT driven by two closely spaced frequency components of opposite circular polarization, showing that when Zeeman splitting matches the frequency difference, a dark state arises for one beam direction, generating a net radiation pressure force.
result: They identify the specific conditions under which the trapping and cooling forces arise, demonstrating that the force is directed toward the field zero.
conclusion: The work provides a clear physical picture of how blue-detuned MOTs work for molecules, which could improve molecular cooling and trapping experiments.

title: Quantum-enhanced T-stochastic Neighbor Embedding For High-dimensional Data Visualization
authors: Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, And Song Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Zhang, Chao-Hua Yu, Gong-De Guo, and Song Lin

t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) is a nonlinear dimensionality reduction algorithm that preserves local similarity by matching probability distributions between high- and low-dimensional spaces. Owing to its ability to capture complex manifold structures, t-SNE has become a widely…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023265] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced version of t-SNE for high-dimensional data visualization using quantum amplitude estimation.
motivation: Classical t-SNE is computationally expensive for large datasets; quantum algorithms may offer speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages amplitude estimation to accelerate the computation of pairwise similarities and gradient descent in t-SNE.
result: The quantum t-SNE achieves a quadratic speedup in the number of data points compared to classical t-SNE, with theoretical analysis and small-scale simulations.
conclusion: Quantum computing can enhance nonlinear dimensionality reduction, but practical implementation remains challenging due to limited qubits and noise.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: Efficient simulation of active matter systems with many particles and steric interactions is computationally challenging.
method: The kinetic event-chain algorithm extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian disks, enabling rejection-free, continuous-time dynamics.
result: The algorithm accurately reproduces the phase behavior and dynamics of active Brownian disks, including motility-induced phase separation.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm provides an efficient and accurate method for simulating active matter systems with steric interactions.

title: Multiobjective Tweezers In Scattering Media
authors: Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, And Romain Fleury
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Nerson, Jakob Hüpfl, Clément Ferise, David Globosits, Marlene Hudler, Matthieu Malléjac, Stefan Rotter, and Romain Fleury

Radiation forces and torques enable the manipulation of objects with acoustic and electromagnetic waves. Yet, harnessing them in complex scattering media remains a formidable challenge, especially when multiple objects must be controlled under competing objectives. Here, we demonstrate that sound or…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023254] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates multi-objective manipulation of particles using acoustic tweezers in complex scattering media.
motivation: Controlling multiple objects with radiation forces in scattering environments is challenging; the authors aim to achieve simultaneous manipulation under competing objectives.
method: They use wavefront shaping and optimization algorithms to generate acoustic fields that trap and move multiple particles independently in a scattering medium.
result: Experimental and numerical results show successful independent control of multiple particles in a highly scattering environment.
conclusion: Multiobjective tweezers enable complex particle manipulation in scattering media, with potential applications in biomedical and microfluidic systems.

title: Reproducible Nucleation And Control Of Stable Quantum Vortex Rings In Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, And Luca Galantucci
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, and Luca Galantucci

Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluid systems under clean and controlled conditions emerges as a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research. This work introduces an experimentally feasible protocol for the on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings in harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates, systematically investigating how the protocol setup influences the ring dynamics and proposing a method to generate vortex excitations such as Kelvin waves.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022043] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a protocol for nucleating and controlling stable quantum vortex rings in Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluids is a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research.
method: The authors propose an experimentally feasible protocol using harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates and systematically investigate how the setup influences ring dynamics.
result: They demonstrate on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings and a method to generate Kelvin waves.
conclusion: The protocol enables controlled studies of vortex dynamics in clean superfluid systems.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, and Alessio Celi

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on the topological properties of the system.
motivation: Topological gauge theories are important for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter, and realizing them on nontrivial topologies reveals their topological properties.
method: The authors propose a cold-atom setup using a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to engineer a synthetic gauge field, effectively encoding a topological gauge theory.
result: The scheme allows the observation of topological effects such as persistent currents and quantized responses in the Bose gas.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for studying topological gauge theories in a controlled cold-atom system, but it is primarily a condensed matter/atomic physics experiment without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, and Markus Heyl

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function for quantum many-body systems, achieving high accuracy on frustrated magnets and dynamics.
motivation: To improve neural network quantum states by incorporating symmetries and attention mechanisms for better representation of quantum wave functions.
method: Proposes a transformer architecture with convolutional layers that respect lattice symmetries, trained via variational Monte Carlo.
result: Sets new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics compared to previous neural network approaches.
conclusion: Convolutional transformer wave functions are a powerful tool for simulating quantum many-body systems, especially where symmetries are important.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts
abstract:
Author(s): Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, and Patrick Emonts

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic techniques for gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS), focusing on gauge fixing and translation invariance in lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative studies but suffer from sign problems in Monte Carlo simulations; tensor network methods offer an alternative, but handling gauge symmetries efficiently is challenging.
method: The authors introduce a gauged Gaussian fermionic PEPS ansatz and propose algorithms for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance, leveraging the Gaussian structure for computational efficiency.
result: They demonstrate that gauge fixing reduces computational cost and that translation invariance can be imposed systematically, enabling simulation of larger systems.
conclusion: The proposed methods advance tensor network simulations of lattice gauge theories, but the work is primarily a computational technique for condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, finding stability near the Curie point.
motivation: To understand the robustness of topological magnon gaps in 2D ferromagnets for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures using a microscopic spin model.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie temperature.
conclusion: The stability suggests potential for designing robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Are Neural Networks Collision Resistant?
authors: Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, And Riccardo Zecchina
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Benedetti, Andrej Bogdanov, Enrico M. Malatesta, Marc Mézard, Gianmarco Perrupato, Alon Rosen, Nikolaj I. Schwartzbach, and Riccardo Zecchina

A study of the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network shows that efficient algorithms fail to find collisions, a result of direct relevance for the definition of new cryptographic protocols based on machine-learning models.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021051] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the computational complexity of finding collisions in a one-layer neural network, showing that efficient algorithms fail, which is relevant for cryptography based on machine learning.
motivation: To understand whether neural networks can serve as collision-resistant hash functions for cryptographic applications.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of finding collisions in a simple one-layer neural network using theoretical and algorithmic approaches.
result: Efficient algorithms are shown to fail to find collisions, suggesting that such neural networks may be collision resistant.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for defining new cryptographic protocols based on machine learning models.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is important but challenging; existing methods often lack physical grounding.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical principles to infer causal links from time-series data of network dynamics.
result: The framework successfully predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: Physics-informed inference can effectively uncover causal structures in networks, with potential applications in many fields.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers near topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers by leveraging topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis using field theory and numerical methods to study the phase diagram and anyonic condensation.
result: Topological criticality enables the formation of anyonic exciton superfluids with unique properties.
conclusion: The work provides a robust mechanism for engineering anyonic superfluids in quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.
motivation: To investigate the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which may host exotic magnetic order.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques to characterize the phase transition.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state, and the transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The study provides evidence for a novel magnetic ground state in kagome ice systems, relevant to frustrated magnetism and topological order.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To find and characterize materials with flat bands that can host strongly correlated electron states at room temperature, which is important for studying exotic quantum phenomena.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic band structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature were observed.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states without the need for cryogenic conditions.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses magneto-optical spectroscopy to probe quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, demonstrating electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To investigate the quantum anomalous Hall phase in twisted bilayer WSe2 and understand the interplay between topology and magnetism in moiré materials.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to probe the electronic structure and magnetic ordering under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: The experiments reveal a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and show that an electric field can switch between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a promising platform for studying topological phases with tunable magnetism, relevant for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the liquid-gas criticality of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on density fluctuations and critical opalescence suppression.
motivation: To understand the unusual critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, which exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and simulations to investigate the critical properties of a model of spinning particles that form a hyperuniform fluid.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show suppressed critical opalescence but enhanced susceptibility at the liquid-vapor critical point.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit a unique type of criticality that combines suppressed fluctuations with high susceptibility, offering new insights into critical phenomena.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, focusing on residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments reveal unexpected scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize the scattering behavior.
result: Residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniform designs for photonic applications and suggest new design rules.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates ballistic spin transport and spin valve behavior in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, a condensed matter physics result with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene via electron optics, enabling gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene devices to observe spin-dependent electron trajectories.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport and a spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for coherent spin control using electron optics, but the work is primarily a condensed matter transport study.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the dipolar nematic state may clarify their behavior.
method: The authors likely use theoretical modeling or experimental characterization to investigate the nematic ordering.
result: Identification of a dipolar nematic phase in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The dipolar nematic state is a key feature of relaxor ferroelectrics, but the paper does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines robotic metamaterial experiments with theoretical modeling to probe the percolation of active forces.
result: Increasing activity can lead to a vanishing macroscopic response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The phenomenon 'more is less' arises from the interplay between activity and percolation in active solids.

title: Physics-Based Factorized Machine Learning For Predicting Ionic Dielectric Tensors
authors: Atsushi Takigawa, Shin Kiyohara, And Yu Kumagai
abstract:
Author(s): Atsushi Takigawa, Shin Kiyohara, and Yu Kumagai

A machine-learning methodology helps screen thousands of candidate oxides to identify materials with excellent dielectric properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021006] Published Tue Apr 07, 2026.
tldr: A machine learning method predicts ionic dielectric tensors of oxides using physics-based factorization.
motivation: To accelerate the discovery of materials with excellent dielectric properties for technological applications.
method: A factorized machine learning model that incorporates physical constraints to predict dielectric tensors from crystal structure data.
result: The method successfully screens thousands of candidate oxides and identifies promising materials with high dielectric constants.
conclusion: Physics-based machine learning can efficiently predict dielectric properties, aiding materials discovery.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant that is hard to compute classically, making it a candidate for quantum advantage. The authors aim to demonstrate an end-to-end quantum algorithm that can be executed on near-term devices.
method: The paper designs a complete pipeline from state preparation to measurement, using a quantum circuit that implements a unitary representation of the braid group. It includes error mitigation and resource estimation for execution on trapped-ion and superconducting qubit platforms.
result: The algorithm is successfully implemented on a trapped-ion quantum processor, showing agreement with classical simulations for small knot instances. Resource estimates suggest that larger instances could outperform classical methods.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for quantum computers and provides insights into the resources required for quantum advantage in topological computation.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors propose a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition to decompose any target photonic state into a sequence of photon catalysis operations, which are experimentally feasible.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The work provides a general and resource-efficient framework for photonic state preparation, advancing photonic quantum computing and quantum optics.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications, including topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and opened new directions.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving with expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology, with potential for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from condensed matter physics.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new electronic states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: Spin glasses are a model system for complex disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics has broad applications.
method: The review synthesizes experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale numerical simulations.
result: Highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation in advancing the field.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich area for future research, with implications for many physical systems.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on material candidates and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in candidate materials, discussing their magnetic properties and topological features.
result: Highlights key materials such as α-RuCl3 and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new experimental or theoretical results.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with many open questions, and the review serves as a guide for future work.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open challenges in accurately modeling internal conversion in complex systems.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to better understand and control internal conversion for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum skyrmion behavior and identifies open questions.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for future quantum technologies, but remains largely exploratory.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their possible mediation by exotic bosons and implications for dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to probe fundamental symmetries through spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and summarizes experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, highlighting the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; further improvements in experimental sensitivity are needed.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A review of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in exotic geometries that are difficult to realize in natural materials, enabling simulation of topological phenomena and models of gravity.
method: The paper surveys experimental and theoretical approaches for implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems.
result: It summarizes progress in realizing synthetic geometries and discusses emergent phenomena like topological states and analogies to gravity.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly growing field with potential for simulating fundamental physics, but it is not directly aligned with the user's core research directions.

title: Role Of Anionic Lone-Pair-Like Electrons In Producing Minimum Lattice Thermal Conductivity
authors: Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, And Zhigang Zou
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Ming, Jiahui Wang, Shike Xu, Bushra Jabar, Yunpeng Zheng, Zhong-Zhen Luo, and Zhigang Zou

Cationic lone-pair electrons are often associated with distinctive phonon properties (e.g., strong lattice anharmonicity) that lead to low lattice thermal conductivity ([MATH]). However, the reliance on specific cations (e.g., [MATH] or [MATH]) severely restri…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236301] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the role of anionic lone-pair-like electrons in achieving minimum lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectric materials.
motivation: To overcome the limitation of relying on specific cations for low lattice thermal conductivity by exploring anionic lone-pair-like electrons.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental measurements to analyze phonon properties and thermal conductivity.
result: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons induce strong lattice anharmonicity, leading to ultralow lattice thermal conductivity.
conclusion: Anionic lone-pair-like electrons provide a new strategy for designing materials with minimum lattice thermal conductivity.

title: Lorentz Violation In Emergent Gravity And Its Cosmological Consequences
authors: Raymond Isichei And João Magueijo
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Isichei and João Magueijo

We show that general relativity and other geometrical theories can be viewed as a degenerate Otto cycle with only heat-exchange legs in emergent gravity. Including work-producing legs yields controlled violations of local Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation, which produce late-time c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 231501] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper interprets general relativity as a degenerate Otto cycle in emergent gravity, leading to Lorentz violation and late-time cosmological acceleration.
motivation: To explore the connection between gravity and thermodynamics, and to derive observable consequences of Lorentz violation from an emergent gravity perspective.
method: The authors model gravity as a thermodynamic cycle (Otto cycle) in the context of emergent gravity, and introduce work-producing legs that break Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation.
result: They find that controlled violations of Lorentz invariance and energy-momentum conservation produce late-time cosmological acceleration, potentially explaining dark energy.
conclusion: The emergent gravity framework with thermodynamic cycles can generate Lorentz violation and cosmic acceleration, offering a new perspective on dark energy.

title: Nanoscale Coherent Phonons With Broadband Frequency Tunability
authors: Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), And Ying Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhengpu Zhao (赵正朴), Da Wu (吴达), Chuwei Zhang (张楚惟), Duanyun Cao (曹端云), Haotian Zheng (郑浩天), Yuqing Huang (黄玉清), Qin Wang (王钦), En-Ge Wang (王恩哥), Chaoyu Guo (郭钞宇), and Ying Jiang (江颖)

Broadband-tunable coherent phonon tips probe functional materials at nanoscale to investigate a variety of optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 236201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates nanoscale coherent phonon tips with broadband frequency tunability for probing functional materials.
motivation: To enable nanoscale investigation of optical, electronic, thermodynamic, and mechanical properties of materials using tunable coherent phonons.
method: The authors develop a tip-based platform that generates and detects coherent phonons with broadband frequency tunability at the nanoscale.

conclusion: The technique provides a new tool for nanoscale characterization of functional materials, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

tldr: This paper presents an acoustic analogy of the quantum Baldin sum rule, demonstrating a trade-off in sound wave scattering across frequencies.

method: Experimental measurements and theoretical modeling of sound wave scattering from engineered structures.
result: Scattering enhancement in one frequency range necessarily reduces scattering in another, confirming the sum rule.
conclusion: The acoustic Baldin sum rule provides a universal constraint for optimal causal scattering, with implications for acoustic engineering.

conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting thermal transport in 2D materials at low temperatures, relevant for nanoelectronics.

result: Evidence for emergent spin-singlet pairing and a quantum-disordered magnetic state is observed.

At small twist angles, two-dimensional moiré materials behave more like elastic membranes than rigid crystals, and structural reconstruction becomes increasingly dramatic as the twist angle decreases. Existing treatments rely on numerical simulations that fail due to the enormous atom count in the moiré cell. method: The authors establish an analytical theory characterized by a single parameter, enabling predictions for twisted bilayer graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides.
result: The theory accurately predicts experimental observations of lattice relaxation in marginally twisted bilayers.
conclusion: The analytical framework provides a scalable method to understand structural reconstruction in moiré materials without heavy numerics.

tldr: Develops a physics-based analytical model for the ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers.
motivation: To understand the phase transition mechanism in a technologically relevant ferroelectric polymer.
method: Constructs a free-energy model based on the Landau-Devonshire theory, incorporating dipole interactions and chain conformations.
result: The model reproduces the temperature dependence of polarization and dielectric constant, and predicts the transition temperature as a function of copolymer composition.
conclusion: The analytical model provides a quantitative description of the ferroelectric transition in P(VDF-TrFE) copolymers, useful for material design.

title: Virtual Cathode Behavior In A Crossed-field Gap
authors: Ashmita Panda, Jim Browning, And Allen L. Garner

While the behavior of virtual cathodes (VCs) in a space-charge limited gap in the absence of a magnetic field is well understood, it is less characterized for crossed-field gaps with perpendicular magnetic and electric fields. Thus, this study examines VC formation at steady state in a crossed-field…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065202] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies virtual cathode formation in crossed-field gaps, a topic in plasma physics and vacuum electronics.
motivation: Understanding virtual cathode behavior in crossed-field gaps is important for high-power microwave devices and vacuum electronics.
method: The authors use steady-state analysis and simulations to examine virtual cathode formation under perpendicular electric and magnetic fields.
result: They characterize the conditions for virtual cathode formation and its properties in crossed-field gaps.
conclusion: The study extends the understanding of virtual cathodes to crossed-field configurations, relevant for device design.

title: Externally Driven Condensates Show Translation-induced Polarization, Directed Coalescence, And Anomalous Diffusion In Viscoelastic Media
authors: Andriy Goychuk

[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase separation in viscoelastic media under external driving, focusing on polarization, coalescence, and anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how external fields and viscoelasticity control the organization of phase-separated domains in soft matter and biological systems.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of externally driven condensates in viscoelastic media.
result: Translation-induced polarization, directed coalescence, and anomalous diffusion are observed.
conclusion: External driving can be used to control domain organization in viscoelastic environments.

title: First-passage-time Properties Of Diffusion With A Broad Class Of Stochastic Diffusion Coefficients
authors: Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, And Hitoshi Washizu
abstract:
Author(s): Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, and Hitoshi Washizu

This study investigates the first-passage-time (FPT) properties of particles with a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients (DCs), representing diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations. We demonstrate that for diffusion in a one-dimen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064108] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in heterogeneous environments.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in heterogeneous media is important for transport in disordered systems and biological processes.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to derive FPT distributions for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
result: The paper characterizes how stochastic diffusion coefficients affect the first-passage-time statistics, revealing universal scaling behaviors.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into diffusion in complex environments but have no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Relative-advection-induced Instability In A Reaction-diffusion-advection System
authors: Chuanjun Dai, Ruyi Zhou, Qing Guo, And Min Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Chuanjun Dai, Ruyi Zhou, Qing Guo, and Min Zhao

The instability mechanism in general reaction-diffusion-advection systems is key to understanding flow-driven self-organization. Here we report the general conditions for instability in [MATH]-dimensional space, formally termed relative advection instability (RAI) given its exclusive dependence on the …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064202] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies instability in reaction-diffusion-advection systems, a topic in nonlinear dynamics and pattern formation.
motivation: Understanding flow-driven self-organization in reaction-diffusion-advection systems is important for biological and chemical pattern formation.
method: The authors derive general conditions for instability in n-dimensional space, termed relative advection instability (RAI), using linear stability analysis.
result: They identify conditions under which advection induces instability, independent of diffusion-driven Turing instability.
conclusion: RAI provides a new mechanism for pattern formation in advective systems, with potential applications in ecology and fluid dynamics.

title: Resetting-induced Instability In Queues Fed By A Search Process In An Interval
authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): José Giral-Barajas and Paul C. Bressloff

Proper management of resources whose arrival and consumption are subject to environmental randomness is an intrinsic process in both natural and artificial systems. This phenomenon can be modeled as a queuing process whose arrival distribution is determined by a search process with stochastic resett…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064101] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a queuing model where arrivals are governed by a search process with stochastic resetting, leading to instability.
motivation: To understand how resetting in search processes affects the stability of queues, which is relevant to resource management in random environments.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a queue fed by a search process on an interval with resetting, deriving conditions for instability.
result: Resetting can induce instability in the queue even when the underlying search process would otherwise be stable.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting can fundamentally alter queue dynamics, with implications for natural and artificial systems.

title: Unveiling Dielectric Relaxation And Shear Rheology In Water
